## Rates service checkpoint (R5, partial)

`crates/rates` owns the shared service independently of either adapter.
`cached_at_or_before` is the pricing/journal lookup API; `latest`, `range`
and `pairs` are local reads. `Sample`/`upsert` retain exact Decimal strings
alongside legacy REAL columns, using `pydecimal` and `pyjson`. Low-level writes
participate in the caller's transaction; `command` supplies the CLI transaction
boundary, including rebuild rollback. `ensure_bundled_seed` imports embedded
Kraken daily/hourly data only when that pair/granularity has no seed. Cache
keys remain `(pair,timestamp,source)` and checked-minute keys also include the
source. This Python base has no rate TTL or interpolation.

Latest selection orders by timestamp, manual preference, fetched time, then
source. Pricing lookup has the same first three terms and intentionally no
source or id tie-break in this base. The insertion tie is independently pinned
against Python. Range ordering, confirmed-time transaction windows, sparse
checked minutes, 300-candle boundaries, finest CSV interval and LBTC-to-BTC
fallback have native tests and the mutation catalog below.

The family modules in `crates/cli` and `crates/daemon` delegate through
`Book::rates`. The daemon advertises `ui.rates.summary`, `ui.rates.coverage`,
`ui.rates.kraken_csv.import` and `ui.rates.latest`. Reads and local imports
do not fetch. Latest requires the active book's market-rate opt-in before
minting an exact-action grant. The [egress reference](rust-port-egress.md#rates-service-paths-r5)
lists each provider path and its no-traffic regression. AI projections remain
in Python.

This checkpoint is **not complete slice acceptance**:

- `ui.rates.rebuild` returns `not_implemented` before mutation or egress and is
  not advertised. Its repricing/journal composition depends on unported services.
- Native tests cover the cache/providers/CSV core, but the entire `rust-test`
  intent inventory is not yet ported. In-process Python daemon tests do not
  prove Rust execution. In particular the journal rollback, desktop rebuild
  and full transaction-pricing preservation scenarios remain open.
- HTTP `Retry-After` currently accepts integer seconds, not HTTP dates. Generic
  upstream error wording still differs: Rust withholds peer response text.
  Nonfinite Decimal inputs fail closed. Full provider error parity remains open.
- Local ZIP ingestion supports stored/DEFLATE ZIP/ZIP64, UTF-8 filenames and a
  1 GiB uncompressed member limit. Python accepts additional compression/name
  encodings. Hostile archive and full-history resource-limit acceptance remains
  open. Bundled data are embedded, but the returned resource display path still
  names the build checkout; installed-binary path parity remains open.
- Desktop context resolution currently expects saved IDs; Python also accepts
  label references. Coverage rejects mismatched workspace/profile IDs and
  latest refuses them before egress. Automatic scheduling is unported: only
  the scoped enabled-refresh service API exists.

`tests/test_rust_rates_candidate.py` explicitly records Rust service for all six
CLI leaves and compares deterministic native daemon summary/coverage/validation
records with Python as raw bytes. The existing CSV subprocess cases and rate
CLI smoke scenarios also run through the hybrid candidate. Direct Python mock
tests remain reference checks until their native replacements are complete.
The native daemon scenario also proves that a failed second CSV member rolls
back the first member's pending writes before the next request.

## Reports AI-provider failure diagnosis (R5 third continuation)

The earlier broader hybrid failure is
`tests/test_cli_smoke.py::CliSmokeTest::test_01b_ai_providers_roundtrip`,
at its first `chat hello --provider smoke-remote` acknowledgement assertion
(line 686 at `89f978ac`). Python alone reproduces the returned error:
`internal_error`, `[Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/home/tg/.kassiber/run'`.
Chat starts its Python daemon, then `_resolve_default_model` requests the
provider list. That request lazily opens the daemon's book and takes ownership
before provider acknowledgement. The ownership guard resolves the account
home through `pwd`, deliberately ignoring `HOME` and XDG overrides, then
creates its stable owner-lock namespace. This sandbox permits
reads there but not directory creation. A disposable book or temporary `HOME`
therefore does not remove the restriction.

Both the Python-only and hybrid executions of that exact smoke test pass with
the owner-lock filesystem access available. The fresh hybrid routing log records
all nine calls in Python: provider list/create/get/update/set-default/
clear-default/delete, `chat`, and `ai.models`. Rust serves none of them; chat's
child daemon is explicitly Python as well. Both acknowledgement refusals pass
before any provider request. This is an environmental filesystem restriction,
not an AI-routing, report-port or harness defect; no Python product fix is
needed. The earlier `secrets init` descriptor-fallback failure has the same
owner-lock directory restriction.

child rows together on failure and preserves an enclosing caller transaction.

resolution rows stay intact; filing does not recalculate or copy impact history.

## XLSX renderer foundation (R5, partial)

The owner decision of 2026-10-31 moves XLSX rendering to
`crates/xlsx` with `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.102.0; PDF remains Python. The isolated
renderer accepts typed workbook content and returns complete bytes in RAM.
It cannot open a book, establish accounting facts, publish a report or file it.
The [plan decision](../plan/21-rust-backend.md#r5-xlsx-owner-decision-2026-10-31)
records dependency features, licenses and deterministic properties.

`tests/rust_port/xlsx.py` records the real Python writer's rendering calls while
independently producing its workbook. `tests/test_rust_xlsx.py` compares that
file with the Rust renderer using openpyxl in formula and cached-value modes.
The canonical dump includes every populated/styled blank cell, all style
properties, typed formula caches, hyperlinks, differential formats, ordered
sheets, dimensions, merges, freeze panes, filters, defined names, margins,
page setup and core document properties. Style/shared-string indices and XML
ordering are structural details, so styles are resolved before comparison.
ZIP checksums, unique members and XML parsing must succeed; openpyxl must load
without warnings. Repeated renders must be byte-identical to each other.

| Renderer parity corpus | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| Full, transactions, Austrian E1kv, year handoff and exit-tax contract books | 5 |
| CoinTracking and Blockpit cross-check workbooks | 2 |
| Inherited export fixtures, including exact pre-render refusals | 197 |
| Empty/boolean/Unicode/formula-like strings, negative/huge/tiny numbers, long text and 2,000 rows | 13 |
| Total | 217 |

Content differences found and resolved: Python rounds ordinary numeric cells
to 16 significant digits but preserves full float text for formula caches;
Rust otherwise writes huge floats as literal integers; Rust quantizes row
heights to integer pixels, collapses explicit empty strings into blanks, and
adds default portrait/200-DPI printer hints. The in-memory ZIP pass preserves
Python's numeric representation, exact point heights and empty string types,
and removes those unsolicited print hints. Bold, widths, formulas, caches,
merges, panes, names and timestamps compare without remaining differences in
this corpus. Container bytes intentionally differ from Python.

The low-level renderer follows each requested merge operation. Report writers
now write a one-column title as a real cell, matching the corrected Python
reference; see the exit-tax checkpoint below.

All six renderer mutations are killed by the named tests in
`crates/xlsx/tests/content.rs`; their catalog and offline scratch-tree runner
live under `crates/xlsx/scripts/`. Renderer fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` and
all six Rust tests pass. Evidence is under `target/xlsx/{parity,mutations}.log`;
the disposable mutation build and source trees are removed after verification.

This is a renderer boundary, not complete XLSX service acceptance. These
tests do not establish native admission or routing for the unregistered XLSX
report commands. Native projections and their CLI/daemon transport, completion
hashes/summaries and explicit filing need separate verification.

## Exit-tax service checkpoint (R5 fourteenth reports continuation, partial)

The native CLI and daemon exit-tax read/XLSX family follows Python reference
rounds 6, 6b, 6c and 6d (`826f01d4f` through `9a3fe17e6`), on top of the
`t3code/r5-reports-16` port. It reports the configured normalized method and
reconstructs historical global inventory and wallet quantities from stored
journal entries. Income is counted once; transfers move wallet context, and
transfer fees are not deducted from that context twice. Consumed-lot markers
precede overrideable disposal categories. Acquisitions use their own regime
marker or date; a disposal category never reclassifies an acquisition.

Austrian departure dates use the Europe/Vienna civil day, including winter,
summer, 23-hour spring and 25-hour autumn days; generic dates use UTC. Timed
inputs require an explicit offset and select the jurisdiction's civil day;
naive times return the same typed validation error and hint. One exclusive
next-midnight instant bounds inventory and both local quote sources. The closest usable cache or
transaction quote strictly before that instant wins, at most 24 elapsed hours
old inclusive. Cache wins equal instants with manual-provider priority. Quote
`asOf` is the source time in UTC Z, retaining microseconds. No rate is acquired
by these reads. Held wallet-only assets are priced too; any missing FMV leaves
aggregate market/gain/tax totals null with explicit incomplete readiness.

The text/PDF projection and XLSX disclose departure timezone, journal input
version and FMV source/time. XLSX adds an FMV quotes worksheet, quarantine and
missing-price warnings, and a real cell title on the one-column Assumptions
sheet. Missing-FMV workbooks remain available as incomplete drafts. Native
PDF publication and AI projections remain on Python. The overview dashboard
Alt flags are not ported natively; Python retains round 6d's per-asset, consumed-lot
wallet flags and Vienna default date. The native wallet-list snapshot exposes
no Alt flag.

Journal builds stamp calculation semantics version 2. The audited
`at-outflow-consumed-regime-v2` migration covers retained Austrian disposals,
fees and transfer fees independently of the older fee-v1 audit. It preserves
observations, authored evidence, journals and saved/filed artifacts while
requiring a rebuild. The adoption audit and processing-marker trigger protect
freshness after an older writer rebuilds, including repeated timestamps.
Native storage and retained-journal readers share this stamp requirement.
The native tax engine splits consumed Alt/Neu fragments before taxability or
category overrides, preserving fee zero-gain behavior and realized overrides.

Exit-tax drafts retain their deliberate exclusion from ordinary realized-report
snapshot/capture registration. Existing saved commitments and pending amendment
history remain unchanged. A replayable valuation snapshot design remains
separate work; a historical bug is no longer a parity target.

Verification commands and local logs are recorded under `target/r5-exit-tax/`.
The regenerated corpus pins every method/jurisdiction, civil-day/DST and quote
boundary, exact values, historical context, null totals, disclosures, stamps,
readiness and refusals. Real service comparisons cover normalized response
bytes, openpyxl workbook content and canonical bytes of all 112 SQLite tables.
Only each independently checked XLSX container byte count is normalized.
Native CLI/daemon scenarios assert zero in-scope Python fallbacks. The native
reviewer matrix pins the independent EUR 65,000 figures with every disposal
override and also retains the original timestamps that put two receipts on
April 1 in Vienna. Mutation catalogs name the native test for each new rule.

## Source-funds frozen-case persistence foundation (R5 partial)

`t3code/r5-sof-mutations` starts at `a99fa77c8`. The native
`source_funds_cases::save_snapshot` helper accepts an already composed
`FrozenCase`; it does not accept a report recipe or establish review approval.
It preserves the two distinct UUIDs, one timestamp, exact integer target msat,
null/empty distinctions, frozen external/recipient fields, sorted spaced
snapshot JSON and the SHA-256 of separately sorted compact JSON. Decimal
values use shared `json_ready` conversion before either serialization.
The case and immutable snapshot carry identical payloads and commitments.
No attachment files are read, copied or written by this persistence step.
Stored evidence and diagrams remain frozen data, without granting ownership,
basis or tax authority.

A savepoint owns both inserts and rolls back failures, including a refused
snapshot insert and a deferred foreign-key or busy refusal at commit. A failed
standalone commit uses full rollback; nested statement failures roll back the
helper's savepoint while retaining the caller's pending work. Python's raw
helper commits its caller's transaction; this composable
helper leaves a nested caller to commit the complete reviewed operation.
The eventual reviewed operation must acquire the write lock, recompute
the native report/fingerprint, call this helper and commit under that same
lock, rolling back the outer transaction if it fails. This helper alone
cannot perform those admission checks.

The raw Python `save_case_snapshot` helper leaves a pending case row after
a later snapshot insert fails. Its caller must roll back. The differential
oracle performs that caller rollback on errors; Python product code is
unchanged. The synthetic reproduction is:

```sh
mise exec rust@1.99.1 uv@latest -- uv run --locked python \
  -m crates.reports.scripts.repro_python_source_funds_cases
```

The reference corpus contains 37 cases: 29 saves and eight refusals. It covers
Unicode/surrogate JSON, nested ordering, float/Decimal conversion, non-finite
snapshot values, exact msat extremes, disclosure modes, recipient rename and
deletion, literal evidence metadata, identity collisions, insert failures and
deferred commit refusal. Receipt success envelopes are compared in their
complete CLI and compact daemon encodings. Those encodings are helper tests,
not registered transport acceptance. Internal failures remain structured
service comparisons; the existing traceback/debug wire gap is not waived.

one of the 112 tables after each operation. Separate disk-backed tests prove
outer-transaction preservation and rollback after a busy commit refusal on

must be positive and is clamped to 500. The outer report savepoint restores
all rows on success, cap refusal and unexpected failure before a result escapes.
The preview never claims committed provenance. It opens no evidence file and
makes no backend/network request.

require zero in-scope fallbacks. Generated process UUIDs have an explicit
one-to-one mapping; the mapping and both raw byte hashes are retained with each
comparison. Every other byte remains literal.

## Not yet ported

The diagnostics slice now implements explicit public reports and native debug
provenance (below). There is no cached update banner, no RAM log
ring or request log, and no operator broker or broker child. A bound brokered
project's commands fail `not_implemented`. The operator protocol, endpoint and
client exist as libraries ([R6-1](#operator-protocol-local-ipc-and-ownership-r6-1))
but nothing registers them yet.

## Reviewed differences

Each is a proposal for review under plan 21's parity rule:

- Legacy project copying refuses an existing held local owner reservation or
  nonempty WAL/rollback journal; Python's copy path lacks these checks. Close
  and checkpoint the source before retrying Rust. This guard does not establish
  full concurrent-copy acceptance.
- `commands describe` resolves no project and creates no layout; Python
  bootstraps (creating the default project) before describing. Only the
  `--project`/`--data-root` conflict is still refused.
- Where Python hangs or crashes, the Rust daemon answers: a request line that
  is not UTF-8 gets `invalid_json` (Python's reader thread dies); JSON nested
  beyond 1,000 levels or an int over 4,300 digits gets `invalid_json` with
  Python's exception text (Python's loop crashes); end of input while
  draining an oversized line, or while the control channel waits, stops the
  daemon (Python polls forever); a second control-channel wait in one request
  examines only new lines (Python spins on its own deferred lines until the
  timeout).
- A `daemon.unlock` passphrase holding lone surrogates is denied
  (`local_auth_denied`); Python fails encoding it.
- Command-line arguments that are not UTF-8 are refused with exit 2; Python
  carries them as surrogate escapes.
- Without `COLUMNS`, usage and help wrap at 80 columns even on a terminal;
  Python asks the terminal for its width. Pipes, which agents and the desktop
  use, wrap at 80 in both.
- Named-user `--output ~user/...`, and current-user forms without a home
  environment variable, fail `internal_error` with `Could not determine home
  directory.` before filesystem changes. R1 does not consult passwd/NSS or
  directory services; refusing these forms prevents writes to literal tilde
  directories. `~` and `~/...` use `HOME` on Unix; Windows ignores `HOME` and
  uses `USERPROFILE`, then `HOMEDRIVE` + `HOMEPATH`, and accepts `~\...` too.
- A panic in a daemon handler answers `internal_error` with the panic message
  and no `debug` text.

### Chain clients and backend probes (R5 partial)

`crates/chain` exposes immutable `Backend` snapshots, `HttpClient::get_json` /
`get_text`, `CoreClient::call`, and `ElectrumClient::connect` / `call` /
`batch_call`. Construction performs local configuration/trust reads only.
Every request requires the matching `kassiber-net::Consent` and an overall
`Instant` deadline. Core and Electrum accept observation methods only; spending,
signing and broadcasting are refused. Bitcoin and Liquid share the same
Esplora/Electrum transports. Wallet scans, observer persistence and AI
projections are not part of this checkpoint.

The native daemon advertises `ui.backends.http.test`, `.electrum.test`,
`.bitcoinrpc.test`, `.btcpay.test` and `.detect_core`. `ProbeConsent` binds the
exact kind, form arguments and book identity. The real-store adapter mints it
only after the explicit daemon request passes unlock/expected-scope checks.
Saved backend reads and startup never grant it. Each HTTP/BTCPay check is one
logical probe; Electrum reuses one version handshake; Core takes one snapshot
with wallet/filter/prune checks. Core detection considers local configuration
only and refuses non-loopback candidates. Credential references contain no
password or cookie contents. A reference bug allowing nested config URL
changes to retain saved Core credentials has a separate regression/fix commit.

There are no backend-test or detect-core CLI leaves in this Python reference's
command catalog. The CLI `daemon` entry serves these kinds; backend CRUD and
BTCPay inspection/setup CLI commands retain their existing dispositions.

`tests/test_rust_chain_candidate.py` compares five probe kinds byte for byte
with Python on the same owned loopback fakes, checks native hybrid routing,
and compares the three direct client APIs using the test-only
`crates/chain/examples/client_fixture.rs` driver. Build that driver after Cargo
workspace tests, alongside the test-harness binary, before running the module:

```sh
mise exec rust@1.99.1 -- cargo build -p kassiber --features test-harness --offline --locked
mise exec rust@1.99.1 -- cargo build -p kassiber-chain --example client_fixture --features test-harness --offline --locked
KASSIBER_RUST_BIN=$PWD/target/debug/kassiber uv run --locked python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_chain_candidate.py
```

Twenty native tests cover refusal, wire shapes, ordered batching, duplicate
IDs, errors, bounded retry, large Core history, prune uncertainty and credential
scope. Twenty checked-in mutations pin protocol, retry, selection and grant
rules in `crates/chain/scripts/mutations.json`.
The fixture and independent attempt observer require the chain crate's explicit
`test-harness` feature. Ordinary workspace tests keep the production binary's
guard refusal intact; the mutation launcher enables and arms the observer.

```sh
KASSIBER_TEST_NO_EGRESS=1 mise exec rust@1.99.1 -- cargo test -p kassiber-chain --features test-harness --offline --locked
mise exec rust@1.99.1 uv@latest -- uv run --locked python crates/chain/scripts/mutation_check.py
```

The chain candidate module's four hybrid daemon sessions have zero Python
fallbacks. The per-kind counts below include offline and input-validation refusals;
the direct fixture driver is tested separately from product dispatch.

This is a partial boundary. Lightning probing remains `not_implemented` rather
than substituting a smaller LND/CLN health request for Python's full snapshot.
Complete differential failure/TLS/proxy coverage and platform/regtest runs

is not claimed byte-identical. Probe HTTP bodies have the reviewed bounded

Unlike Python's prefix-only read, the current native HTTP probe buffers the

## Read-path performance

Rust read commands retain their existing output and admission contracts while
avoiding fresh-schema reconstruction and redundant compatibility DDL on current
books. Report admission omits review-only inventory serialization, reuses neutral
wallet/asset evidence within its snapshot, streams holdings quote candidates,
and avoids unused capital-gains presentation in summary. No network, schema,
dependency or accounting-policy changes are introduced. The
[read-path report](rust-read-performance.md) records release measurements,
startup spans, verification and remaining costs.

The [second performance round](rust-read-performance-round2.md) adds streaming
admission/history/summary projections, reusable row conversion, exact integer
amount scaling and narrow transaction-page selection. It records phase spans
and scratch index measurements; schema proposals remain unimplemented.
## Diagnostics service slice (R5)

`crates/diagnostics` owns `diagnostics collect`, optional `--save`, and the
explicit global `--diagnostics-out PATH|auto` error export. The CLI has one
family adapter; the reference has no diagnostics daemon kind or separate AI
projection. Error collection uses the admitted book before it closes. Failures
before admission report unavailable state. A report-write failure is best effort:
it emits Python's redacted stderr notice and preserves the original error.
No automatic log, network request, provider probe, descriptor dispatch or new
AI authority is introduced.

The ordered report schema, argument classes, sensitive-key tokens, fourteen
ordered text rules, recursive detail shapes, aggregate SQL summaries and
syntactic backend locality follow `kassiber/diagnostics.py`. The implementation
reuses the already locked regex engine because CPython lookarounds and Unicode
case/word/space/digit matching are not available in the standard library.
The same existing `nix` dependency supplies public OS identity on Unix; no new
third-party package is introduced.

Native provenance is an owner-approved exception to byte parity. Historical
schema keys `environment.python_version` and `python_implementation` contain
the actual compiler identity and `Rust`, respectively; `sqlite_version` is the
native linked SQLite version. Platform values describe the running host.
The report's `stack` is an empty array on failure: a meaningful bounded public
native trace is unavailable, so Python frames are never fabricated and native
Debug/Display backtraces are never serialized. The CLI envelope always retains
`error.debug` in its original position: it is null without `--debug`, including
for unhandled failures, and an empty string with `--debug`. No native frame
paths, usernames, home directories, build-machine paths or stack locals escape.
An empty stack/debug has zero frames and bytes, below Python's 20-frame report
cap and traceback-size cap.

The report oracle normalizes only `environment.python_version`,
`environment.python_implementation`, `environment.sqlite_version`, and `stack`.
A separate unhandled diagnostics-export envelope oracle normalizes only
`error.debug` when it is a string. Scope regressions prove other values and
layout remain observable. Clocks are injected on both sides in tests, rather
than normalized. The timestamp hook is compiled only into test-harness builds.
All other keys, ordering, nesting, types, bytes, errors and saved-file modes
remain the reference's. Python product code is unchanged.

Python currently uses `Path.write_text` directly, with ordinary umask-derived
permissions, rather than an atomic replacement or an explicit private mode.
Rust deliberately preserves this behavior, including existing-inode/mode
retention. The report filename also follows Python's timestamp sanitizer:
ordinary timestamps produce `kassiber-diagnostics--timestamp-.json`, so a
later automatic export overwrites that filename. These reference limitations
are recorded, not silently fixed in the port.

The checked-in oracle corpus has 29 text cases, 135 sensitive-key cases,
140 recursive detail cases, four argument-class cases, a planted aggregate
state fixture and 146 backend locality vectors. The mutation catalog covers
all fourteen text rules, every sensitive key, native report/debug frame
refusal, debug presence, detail shapes and effective review selection.
See [slice acceptance](rust-diagnostics-r5-status.md) for verification,
served-by evidence, reference repros and platform limits.

The preceding checkpoint implements all five group (a) commands and five of the
fourteen group (b) commands through `crates/transfers`: **9/25 transfers and
1/4 review CLI leaves**, with **9 desktop kinds**. The complete classification
is **(a) 5, (b) 14, (c) 10**. Pair/payout selection uses
persisted effective memberships, never the compatibility pair tables or a new
ownership inference. Split allocations take precedence over review source
amounts. Gap history exposes bounded redacted review facts. Historical receipt
verification never establishes current readiness. Rules are configuration:
invalid stored rules are projected disabled with Python's validation reason.

and default policy selection are shared domain rules; they do not select or
match observations. Stored predicates use `crates/pyjson` sorted-key Python JSON.
Asset normalization uses the locked reference's Unicode 14 uppercase mappings,
including expansions and characters assigned only after that Unicode release.
An invalid stored rule cannot be enabled. Dismissals resolve profile-scoped
transaction IDs before external IDs and refuse ambiguous external references.
Repeated dismissals retain identity/creation time and coalesce absent reasons.
Positive expiry days preserve Python conversion and datetime overflow limits;
explicit CLI zero never expires, while desktop zero retains Python's 90-day
default. Each write owns a savepoint and preserves a caller's transaction.

The deterministic authoring oracle compares **41 sequential operations: 11
successful writes and 30 refusals**. After every operation it compares the
complete rules, dismissals and profile rows as Python JSON bytes, including
stored JSON strings, UUIDs and timestamps injected through a native test-only
source. Every other application table must remain unchanged. Production UUIDs
and time have no environment overrides. Neither rule configuration nor advisory
dismissals invalidates journals or establishes observation, ownership, custody,
basis or provenance facts.

As in the existing shell contract, unexpected Python exceptions include
interpreter-specific traceback text which Rust does not fabricate. The daemon
oracle normalizes only that `error.debug` field for internal errors, plus
production UUID/time fields; error codes/messages and stored bytes remain pinned.

### Pair revision verification

Final verification used Rust 1.99.1, locked Python 3.11, Cargo `--offline`, and
disposable books. Workspace formatting, workspace clippy and the harness-feature
clippy with `-D warnings` passed. `cargo test --offline --workspace --locked`
passed **948 tests**. The final four pair tests also passed against the expanded
115-operation oracle, and the harness build passed. The seven real-process
transfer tests plus the 29-test reference regression module passed **36 tests**.
The exact requested shell/parity/hybrid-candidate/CLI-runner/`tests/rust_port`
gate passed **63 tests and 178 subtests**, including inventory and contracts.
The refreshed error-code snapshot changes source locations only.

All **131 mutations** were killed in a fresh isolated build target after all
**19 named baseline selections** passed. Initial mutation survivors exposed
missing oracle scenarios for unsplit separate swap fees, independent active
memberships and partial group residuals; all were added before the final full
run. The common activation regression also invokes the native helper directly
so the outer pair-service savepoint cannot hide its mutation. Transfer and
shared custody applicability checks passed (131 and 318 entries respectively).

The seven affected hybrid modules passed **386 tests and 35 subtests**, with
one inherited failure:
`ReviewRegressionTest.test_diagnostics_out_auto_writes_public_error_report`.
The global `--diagnostics-out` flag still returns `not_implemented` as it did
at the base checkpoint. This broader run is not reported green. Its 27 calls
to the supported transfer/review subset were all served by Rust, including
pair 6 and unpair 1; the focused witness covers update 2 as well. No supported
command fell back to Python. Group (c) calls intentionally used Python in the
hybrid candidate. Direct native daemon sessions have no Python dispatch.

Sandbox setup hit a quota error under `/tmp`, so disposable roots moved to the
workspace and then memory-backed temporary storage. Early checks also exposed
an unreviewed direct hash dependency, test-tree source-scan pollution, daemon
capability order, a direct Python CLI construction in a test and stale contract
line locations; each was resolved before the final gates. Final Cargo builds
were completed before process tests; mutation builds used a separate fresh
target to avoid reusing mutated artifacts. No push or PR was performed.


### Payout deletion checkpoint

`transfers payouts delete` and `ui.transfers.payouts.delete` now supersede the
stored payout component, preserve immutable terms/evidence, rebuild effective
memberships and perform Python's two journal invalidations. Repeats return the
original deletion time without changing rows. The service owns a savepoint and
preserves an outer caller transaction, including on late invalidation failure.
Desktop input preserves Python truthiness, identifier string conversion and GUI
audit attribution. AI projections remain Python. This brings the supported
subset to **14/29 CLI leaves and 13 desktop kinds**.

| Parity boundary | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Service outputs and normalized database rows | `payout_deletions_match_python_complete_database_rows_and_refusals`: six scenarios, 24 operations; every unrelated application table unchanged |
| CLI bytes and hybrid dispatch | `test_payout_delete_cli_daemon_and_hybrid_bytes`: three calls, all Rust, zero Python fallbacks |
| Daemon bytes | Same test: six requests including repeats, missing/false/numeric IDs and untrusted source |
| Rollback and caller transaction | `payout_deletion_rolls_back_late_failure_and_preserves_outer_transaction` |
| Desktop validation and source | `desktop_payout_delete_requires_id_and_overrides_source` |

The oracle generator is `crates/transfers/scripts/export_payout_delete.py`.
Payout creation is Python-only setup. Its SQL replay pins the exact starting
trigger counters and proves the replayed application rows equal Python before
deletion. Every changed table is compared completely after each operation;
all unrelated tables must stay unchanged in the native runner. No output
UUIDs, timestamps, hashes or array orders are masked. Real-process byte checks
use a stored deletion timestamp; first deletion timestamps and persisted bytes
are checked by the fixed-source native oracle.

The Python savepoint atomicity fix (`ba651df7`, cherry-picked as `be959dd6`)
now makes late payout invalidation rollback match Rust. The deletion oracle's
`late-failure` scenario rejects the second input-version increment and compares
every application table with its pre-operation state after caller rollback.
The old payout-delete bug repro is retired; this path is failure-path parity.

Payout creation, component plan/apply and gap plan/apply remain unported.
The ten computation-dependent commands and the additional desktop kinds listed
above also remain unported. Automatic transfer pairing during journal processing
belongs to R4; no matcher or journal behavior changes here.

### Savepoint reference-fix parity checkpoint

The local `t3code/r5-transfers-5` continuation starts at `b3721292` and
cherry-picks the Python atomicity fix `ba651df7` as `be959dd6`. The cherry-pick
had one documentation conflict; its unrelated dependency-origin context is
excluded from this branch's database compatibility notes.

The two payout rollback repro scripts are retired. Both fixed-source exporters
now inject a refusal of the final, second journal-input-version increment,
assert that Python leaves every application table unchanged after caller
rollback, and export the exact failure response and complete normalized rows
for Rust. Trigger refusal text now survives the transfer service error adapter;
it does not expose SQL statements or connection details, and the shell still

Rust matches both behaviors byte for byte.

### Bitcoin compatibility discovery (R5 preparation only)

`crates/wallets::scan` ports Python's
`discover_compatibility_descriptor_targets` for Bitcoin descriptors. It derives
every receive/change/script-family branch with the existing descriptor code,
retains known-used prefixes, resets the unused streak on history, stops retained
targets at the gap and counts full probed batches in progress. Fixed and
gap-one branches retain only index zero, matching Python. Esplora uses at most
eight HTTP workers; Electrum batches script subscriptions and preserves every
non-null cached status. Both return Python's empty discovery `history_cache`.

Immutable action grants bind exact inputs and scope, are revocable and
single-use, and pass through the existing network gate. Cancellation is checked
around protocol/derivation batches and before returning targets; an in-flight
request keeps its overall deadline. No database, ownership, custody or journal
API is called. Out-of-range index checkpoints and malformed counters refuse
with fixed diagnostics rather than hiding possible history.

guarded `discovery_fixture` example on the same loopback servers. Each fixture

### Bitcoin protocol acquisition (R5 preparation only)

The continuation in `crates/wallets::acquisition` adds request-local Bitcoin
protocol acquisition. Esplora fetches statistics before/after paginated
confirmed and mempool history, raw UTXOs and an optional tip. Electrum fetches
subscriptions, histories, listunspent, raw transactions and distinct parent
transactions, raw block headers/timestamps and an optional tip. Both return
per-script history and raw observations. Electrum decoding uses integer
satoshis and preserves witness, locktime, sequence, size/vsize/weight and
Python's version-one inline-prevout graph shape. Coinbase null outpoints are
never fetched or given a prevout. Unknown/unavailable/behind tips do not create
a zero confirmation count.

Construction is inert; separate acquisition grants bind immutable targets,
backend route/trust/auth and database/profile/wallet/environment/source scope.
They are revocable and single-use. Offline/unavailable policy refuses even an
empty target list. Cancellation is checked between pages/protocol batches and
before returning. The helper does not reuse observer checkpoints or graph
caches, select canonical transactions, compose normalized accounting records,
or write any durable state. Ordinary Electrum still needs BDK's observer state
and rebuild rules; this helper does not substitute a compatibility observer.

The shared backend parser also refuses non-string configured proxy values.
Previously those values could be treated as absent and select a direct route;
the new constructor regression and mutation pin refusal before I/O.

### Bitcoin observer state and record reuse (R5 partial step 1)

This continuation starts at `711bf220` on local branch `t3code/r5-sync-3`.
It completes an inert state/reuse library checkpoint **within step 1**; it
does not complete step 1 or enable sync. `crates/wallets::observer_state`
normalizes the full version-one BDK aggregate JSON: descriptors/network,
local-chain changes (including removals), serialized witness transactions,
prevouts, anchors, first/last-seen and last-evicted times, revealed descriptor
indices and locked outpoints. BDK's serialized hash byte order and exact
integer satoshis survive. Existing Bitcoin/miniscript dependencies suffice
for this representation boundary; no dependency or lockfile changes are made.
The helper does not merge aggregates or construct a BDK wallet. Local-chain,
transaction and anchor lists preserve duplicates; anchor sorting is stable and
excludes confirmation time. Hex decoding follows Python's byte boundaries,
including ASCII whitespace between bytes, and descriptor extended keys must
match the aggregate's network kind (an absent network selects test keys).

The native translator follows the pinned Electrum point-of-agreement walk,

### Bitcoin normalized record composition (R5 continuation)

This continuation starts at `0da3346b` on local branch `t3code/r5-sync-6`.
It completes this run's numbered step 1, the record-composition part of the
previous handoff's step 3. It stops before atomic persistence and registration.

`crates/wallets/src/bitcoin_records.rs` ports Bitcoin graph record composition
for Esplora-shaped observations (including BDK) and already decoded, normalized
Electrum graphs. It preserves exact sats and Python decimal BTC text, principal
versus fee, collaborative wallet deltas, graph-scoped owned scripts, explicit
privacy boundaries, first-seen/confirmation timestamps and single-outpoint HTLC
claims/refunds. Script/witness evidence remains an observation, with no custody
or tax interpretation. The sync witness field and the minimum decoded-item
count match Python even when malformed hex items are skipped; an alternate
importer witness field grants no HTLC evidence. Malformed graph containers
refuse before projecting related outputs. Raw graph JSON uses Python's sorted
keys and separators.
Electrum's legacy decoder Decimal metadata keeps Python's float JSON spelling;
the accounting quantities still use integral values.

`bdk::Prepared::records` projects only `Wallet::transactions()` canonical
history, resolving aggregate transaction outputs and floating prevouts. An owned
spend whose network fee cannot be proved fails `observer_accounting_ambiguous`.
Fingerprints retain every reference input and omit depth; confirmed record reuse
requires the same release and current stored proof, and fresh/forced/reorg scans
disable it independently of the caller. The result is private JSON records,
fingerprints and a reused-record count, with no durable write.

`composition::compose` implements the reference coordinator's record merge:

- BDK script-family records for one txid are normalized once against the union
  of observed owned scripts. The richest graph supplies metadata; equal scores
  retain the first candidate. Complementary prevouts merge by exact input
  identity; inconsistent inputs and contradictory prevouts fail closed.
- Non-BDK record keys retain their first observation. Dependency and
  compatibility projections cannot be mixed, including an empty compatibility
  inventory snapshot. An empty observer output list remains authoritative;
  duplicate outpoints use the final projection in the original output order.
- Every live normalized record vetoes a retraction from another observer.
  Canonical txid comparison trims Python whitespace and ignores hex case;
  literal non-txid identifiers retain their case. Remaining retractions retain
  observer order and are deduplicated.
- Checkpoints stay keyed by structural observer identity, highest-used indices
  combine by maximum, reuse counts sum, and unrelated checkpoint metadata stays
  intact. Private provenance mappings follow Python's exact-key precedence and
  txid fallback when cross-family normalization changes a record direction.

The pure `records_fixture` driver is test-harness-only. Its 67 checked-in vectors

The reviewed reorg fixture exposed an unchanged-Python reference bug: Esplora's
compatibility route reuses its cache when script statistics are unchanged even
after a confirmed transaction moves to another block. Incremental sync reports
success with zero fetched records, leaves confirmation evidence stale and
appends no saved-report impact. A force-full refresh fetches the changed record
and appends one impact. Rust publication preserves that prepared-fetch outcome;
it does not manufacture evidence the fetch never supplied. The checked-in
reproducer uses only synthetic books and an owned loopback server:

```sh
uv run --locked python -m tests.rust_port.repro_esplora_reorg_cache
```

in `target/r5-sync-10-artifacts/esplora-reorg-repro.json`. Python is not fixed in
this continuation. The reviewed-book test explicitly pins the reference's
zero-impact incremental outcome on Esplora, while requiring impacts for
Electrum's reorg and both protocols' retraction/mempool cases.

#### Review integration handoff

At the transfers-9 checkpoint, R4-9 (`t3code/r4-9-loader`) and R4-12
(`t3code/r4-12-persist`) were parallel, unavailable prerequisites. The following
were requested adapter signatures, **not exports at that checkpoint**. The
[transfers-10 continuation](#native-review-build-assembly-r5-transfers-10-partial)
below records the now-present loader/writer and test-only build assembly. The
workflow transaction, authority and parity requirements in this handoff remain.
The requested signatures used that checkpoint's snapshot and render types:

```rust
use kassiber_custody::snapshot::Snapshot;
use kassiber_envelope::AppError;
use kassiber_journals::JournalState;
use kassiber_pyjson::Value;
use kassiber_store::rusqlite::Connection;

// R4-9: load all facts from this exact connection and its current transaction.
fn load_custody_snapshot(
    conn: &Connection,
    profile: &Value,
    as_of: &str,
) -> Result<Snapshot, AppError>;

// R4-12: store this composed state in the caller's transaction; never commit.
// Return the same summary as Python store_ledger_state, including processed_at.
fn store_ledger_state(
    conn: &Connection,
    profile: &Value,
    state: &JournalState<'_>,
    created_at: &str,
    uuid: &mut dyn FnMut() -> Result<String, AppError>,
) -> Result<Value, AppError>;
```

Both boundaries must preserve every SQLite storage class and exact scalar.
Loading includes book-network admission facts, full ownership/receipt-source
facts and the ordered bounded gap worklist. It must see uncommitted operations
on the supplied connection. It must neither bootstrap another connection nor
repair, sync, price, auto-pair or write. Compose through the existing custody,
fusion and renderer once those are joined; keep the custody projection alive
while the borrowed `JournalState` is used. Retain the existing fail-closed
render admission rather than making a lossy state conversion.

The review adapter must deduplicate quarantines with Python's primary-reason
precedence and remove synthetic/non-live transaction IDs before building cases
or economic effects. Its canonical state must retain entries, whole-book
holdings/tax summary, component blockers and quantity decisions, including each
suspense decision's component provenance. Acquisition operations additionally
need policy-bound economic effects. A count-only projection is insufficient.

Transaction ownership must follow `core/review_workflow.py`:

1. Cases use a consistent read transaction, rolling back only one they own.
   Cursor scope includes profile, input version and `last_processed_at`.
2. Plan makes a same-binding in-memory backup, with an ephemeral SQLCipher
   destination key when needed. Reject an active source write transaction
   without committing it. All operation writes and rebuilds target the clone;
   the live connection's rows and `total_changes` stay unchanged.
3. Apply acquires `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` only if it owns the transaction, enters a
   savepoint and reserves the writer with the profile's no-op version update.
   An existing idempotency key is checked before input freshness: the same
   digest returns its historical receipt, while another digest is refused.
4. Recompute before effects, apply ordered operations, recompute after effects,
   compare the reviewed artifact, call the canonical writer, then insert the
   receipt in that same savepoint. Preserve an outer caller transaction and
   roll back every domain/journal/audit/impact/receipt row on any late failure.
   Any scoped journal cache-size adjustment must be restored after success or
   failure. Commit only at the owning service boundary.

A single captured before/after ledger pair cannot implement all batch paths.
`_apply_operations` rebuilds again when a non-unpair operation precedes an
unpair, then reads the new pair fingerprint and the component's live suspense
decisions. Sibling unpairs retain the original baseline while their shared
component is re-sliced. A snapshot-only shim would either miss that transition
or require an unimplemented composer callback. Applied database parity also
needs the real writer's rows and failure points; replaying expected writes
would not prove its behavior. Transfers-9 stopped after registration and made
**no review-only library port or parity claim**. The native assembler continuation
below is a separate partial checkpoint.

The follow-up must capture Python states at each real `_build` invocation and
compare artifacts, cursor pages, economic digests, refusal precedence and
complete normalized DB dumps. Include mixed metadata/component batches,
interleaved unpairs, stale fingerprints/effects, SQLCipher clone isolation,
idempotent retries after book changes, caller-owned transactions, and injected
failures during operation N, journal storage and receipt insertion. AI
projections must read the resulting native history/receipts unchanged. Only
then register the three review leaves and their three daemon kinds.

`review_workflow::apply` is implemented behind the existing `test-harness` gate.
Portable artifact admission precedes writer acquisition. An autocommit caller
gets `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; every caller gets a nested savepoint and an explicit
writer reservation before receipt lookup. A matching historical key/digest
returns the original receipt before freshness or rebuilding, even after policy,
observations or the input version change. Another digest on that key refuses.
The writer reservation retains Python's existing chain-index trigger effects
on historical retries; idempotency does not mean zero SQL statements.

A fresh execution validates the input version and canonical before effects,
runs the existing ordered metadata/component/unpair services, recomputes after
effects, then calls the existing canonical journal writer. Pending saved/filed
impacts resolve only when that stored journal is report-ready. The durable
receipt includes the exact author, operation results, all affected anchors,
proposed-operation summaries, processed timestamp and verified effects.
`commit=False` leaves success pending, including when apply opened the enclosing
transaction. Failure restores the operation savepoint without discarding earlier
caller edits. Commit failure after savepoint release rolls back the enclosing
transaction. The connection's cache size, synchronous level and spill setting
are checked on both database bindings.

amounts, author strings, timestamps, hashes and other fields are not masked.
The exact clock is supplied only by the test harness. The exporter patches the
filed-report resolution clock as well as the review/storage clocks.

### Review workflow routes (R5 review-1)

Branch `t3code/r5-review-1` starts at `4844ba8b8` with the test-isolation fix
`47a58f4c4`. It brings in the shared desktop parity harness
`tests/rust_desktop_parity.py` from `3d36e8909` as a file, without that branch's
product changes. The review library from transfers-10 to transfers-17 is now
compiled in production builds; `pipeline`, `review_*` and the transfer review
modules are no longer behind `test-harness`. One composition root,
`kassiber_journals::review_workflow::execute`, serves the CLI and the daemon
through the new `Book::review` seam. No Python product code, AI projection,
consent path or dependency changes.

| Route | CLI leaf | Daemon kind | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current cases | `review cases` | `ui.review.cases` | none; one read snapshot |
| Input request | — | `ui.review.request_input` | none; one read snapshot |
| Plan | `review plan` | `ui.review.plan` | none; RAM copy only |
| Apply | `review apply` | `ui.review.apply` | one savepoint, authored `cli` / `gui` |
| Receipt | `review receipt` | `ui.review.receipt` | none |

`ui.review.request_input` is new native code. It checks action, case IDs,
explanation and the bound input version in Python's order. Inside one read
snapshot it requires each case to be current, then returns the sorted packet and
its content digest. The digest is a correlation ID and grants nothing. The
daemon adapter keeps `_review_workflow_payload`'s allowlists: unknown fields
refuse before missing required ones, and both refuse before the book is touched.
The CLI resolves the scope before reading an input file, as Python does. It keeps
the one-million-byte bound, CPython's JSON encoding detection, the
operations-object and plan-envelope unwrapping, and the unhashable-kind
`internal_error`. Non-AppError reference failures map to the daemon's unhandled
envelope.

Plans stay bound to the book's input version and simulate on an in-RAM copy, so
stale plans refuse. Apply admits the stored artifact before taking the writer.
A repeated idempotency key with the same digest returns the stored receipt; a
different digest refuses. Otherwise apply revalidates version and effects,
applies the operations, stores journals and inserts the receipt in one
savepoint, so any refusal or failure leaves every table unchanged. Observed
transactions, reviewed custody and tax facts stay separate; an unresolved
custody case refuses instead of becoming a guessed taxable event.

The process comparisons found one transport difference, now fixed: native
receipts listed `transaction_ids` before `operations`. The library corpus had
compared sorted JSON, so it missed this.
`review_apply_receipts_keep_python_transport_key_order` pins the order.

**Clock.** Each request samples the build clock once (`now_precise`); Python
samples it at each `_build`. Within one request, the two can differ only when a
time-dependent review state, such as a dismissal expiry, falls between two
builds of the same request.

### Bitcoin native fetch assembly (R5)

Branch `t3code/r5-sync-11` starts at `6af84154`. This checkpoint implements
native preparation for the publication coordinator, without product route
registration. `wallets::fetch::Fetch::new` captures the wallet/configuration,
book network, finite local discovery horizon, freshness checkpoint, observer
epochs and closed reuse evidence. It requires autocommit and performs no
transport or writes. Its request-local grant binds that immutable action;
discovery, acquisition and BDK inherit the same revocable `kassiber-net` grant.
Missing/foreign/revoked grants, changed scope, offline and cancellation refuse
without DNS, connection or HTTP metadata. A failed transport attempt consumes
the grant, so retrying requires another explicit action.

The supported scope remains a profile's sole Bitcoin descriptor/xpub wallet,
with a named ordinary Electrum or Esplora backend. Samourai, alternate source
routes, enrichment, other backend kinds and unverified compatibility transport
shapes refuse locally. The latter include proxy/onion, custom CA, serialized
backend configuration and Esplora custom authentication/timeout/TLS reasons.
Operator-pinned HTTPS CA overrides also refuse. These need their own route
witnesses before widening support. The caller still owns current product
scope/configuration validation and cancellation integration; no saved backend
or checkpoint supplies consent.

`bdk::Prepared::update` assembles the complete private aggregate and release-
bound fingerprint map, canonical membership/retractions, transaction records,
unspent-output snapshot, actual revealed coverage and highest-use checkpoint.
Reused records never suppress the output or coverage snapshot. Record order
matches bdkpython's descending chain positions; the raw Rust iterator does not
provide that presentation order. Esplora joins compatibility discovery,
source-bound cached acquisition, exact output facts and the named
`http_route_policy` metadata. Its tip read occurs after history and before
UTXOs. Invalid output amounts and missing inventory containers refuse.

The guarded `publication_fixture` now accepts `native_backend` to prepare its
own fetch from the disposable book, then publish it under the existing fenced
savepoint. The oracle supplies only fixture backend configuration and test
clock/identity seams; it supplies no Python-prepared records, observer state,
output inventory or coverage. Every round starts another Rust process and
opens the book anew. Python uses unchanged product preparation/application;
only BDK's public request clock is frozen. The preflight-race backend is reset
to the same starting state before each implementation observes its race.
Tests compare the entire serialized fetch and canonical bytes of every
table's logical rows, retaining numeric types and array order. As in the
previous publication oracle, elapsed wall time is normalized to zero and
publication identities/timestamps use deterministic seams.

selection through its drop. Competing admission returns Python's retryable

### Bitcoin wallet-sync native graph worker (R5, partial)

Local branch `t3code/r5-sync-21` starts at `821b481a3`. Native graph lookup now
consumes private successful-sync grants through a guarded, explicitly started
daemon worker. This checkpoint does not register product routes or enable
automatic worker startup.

The lookup service reuses local transaction and acquired-observation references
only when their physical facts and network scope agree. Inspection is capped at
256 matching transaction rows. Complete/local/cached graphs, conflicting or
over-limit references, incompatible book scope, Liquid and confidential graphs
cannot initiate Bitcoin lookup. Cache reads bind schema, chain, network and
transaction identity; legacy entries with missing coinbase identity are ignored.
Malformed explicit row transaction IDs cannot fall back to another row identity.

Esplora and Electrum use only `kassiber-chain` and `kassiber-net`, with the synced
wallet's captured backend and proxy configuration. Esplora graph URLs receive
Python's `/api` normalization. There is no alternate-backend fallback. Each
lookup has a ten-second transport deadline and five-second backend timeout cap.
A pass scans at most 1,000 rows, attempts at most 50 graphs, reserves at most 250
uncached prevouts and stops admitting rows after 30 seconds. Electrum prevouts
are deduplicated and fetched in bounded batches; authority is rechecked between
batches, around HTTP retries and before every cache write. Only sanitized public
references enter the existing cache. The private cursor advances failed rows
and leaves a budget-refused row first for the next pass. Job results expose
counts, without the cursor or transport checkpoints.

Prevout inspection checks cancellation and the deadline within its local walk,
deduplicates with a set and stops at the per-transaction missing-parent cap
before reserving the pass-wide budget or fetching parents.

The guarded differential driver fixes only the pass-admission clock in both
implementations. This isolates row/transaction/prevout cursor tests from shared
host load and debug-build cache-write speed. Production retains the real
monotonic clock, and driver transport deadlines and timeouts remain real.

The worker consumes only the receipt-backed mailbox. It opens its own book
inside its thread, takes one temporary SQLCipher session secret and drops that
secret immediately after open. Graph work has its own execution slot; foreground
recovery cannot steal its running job. Request cancellation/revocation and
offline changes remain live; switch, lock, shutdown and EOF cancel and join the
connection owner before acknowledgement or ownership release. Failed connection
close retains the book for retry. Completion emits unsolicited
`ui.freshness.background`; open/run failures emit fixed, redacted
`ui.freshness.worker` categories. A failed event write returns to the request
loop, discards queued authority and terminates after worker cleanup.

The guarded start kind is absent from production and renderer/AI allowlists.
Starting it with no live grant, including after restart with a saved running
graph job, performs no lookup or recovery. The existing handoff inspection
tests retain their inert mailbox until the worker is explicitly enabled. No
dependency or Python product code changes.

Python now shares the cancellation and checkpoint-redaction fences. A separate
correctness deviation has a disposable repro:
`test_reference_electrum_mismatched_transaction_repro_and_native_refusal` shows
that Python assigns the requested transaction ID to different Electrum bytes
and caches the unrelated graph. Native decoding verifies the computed ID and
refuses both mismatched current transactions and parents. Python is unchanged.

The exact remaining handoff is:

1. Integrate automatic mailbox consumption with the eventual native product
   request lifecycle, retaining the terminal-flush barrier and all graph/source
   controls. The current explicitly started guarded worker is the tested seam;
   product startup, complete product envelopes/events and the broader
   restart/reviewed-book corpus remain unaccepted. Do not call the original
   graph step or R5 complete on this evidence alone.
2. Implement product argument validation and inert whole-invocation hybrid
   selection for explicit no-refresh variants, including protocol request-ID
   shapes. Defaults stay on Python. No Python journal bridge or native journal
   refresh is introduced; native refresh still requires R4-13.
3. Prove full product daemon envelopes, event streams and every normalized table
   over disposable Electrum/Esplora fixture, restart and reviewed-book scenarios.
   Require zero served-shape fallbacks and the remaining mutations, then register
   only passing no-refresh shapes and record served-by counts.

empty and lone-surrogate IDs decline the entire invocation. Defaults decline
even when another argument is invalid. Selection requires an already opened
daemon book; unopened, missing and locked books decline without opening,
creating or migrating a database. On admitted current-schema books, selection
changes no logical rows and initiates no backend traffic.

currently admit only integer and boolean representations. Expected scope is
checked separately and removed before argument validation. Enabled unported
sources decline before consent; disabled rate policy remains effective even
with `rates:true`. Wallet sync also
declines paused or empty source selections because Python can use its separate
direct-sync path in those cases. Execution never retries through Python.

## Generic-ledger core and CLI ingestion (R5 continuation)

Native `wallets import-ledger` reads CSV/TSV and XLSX/XLSM files. Native
ledger headers, inferred columns and supplied maps retain exact Bitcoin/sats
amounts, cash and network fees, fiat execution values, types, notes,
counterparties and swap-linkage fields. Original supplied maps are saved with
the import batch; type-map keys retain insertion order before normalization.
`--dry-run` previews every accepted/rejected row without opening a book, even
when supplied wallet/profile/workspace selections do not exist. Inline and
`@path` maps share the reference admission order.

The bounded ZIP reader uses stored or DEFLATE members in memory and never
extracts files. Entry count, individual and total expansion, compression ratio,
CRC, local-header identity and overlap, XML nesting/node count, namespace and
attribute copies, repeated shared strings and workbook-wide rectangular cells
are checked. The [imports reference](imports.md#generic-ledger-import) records the
limits. Workbook selection, shared/inline rich strings, typed cells, cached
formulas, dates and the 1904 epoch follow the frozen Python examples.
Malformed worksheet XML and typed cells retain the reference error boundary.

The corpus contains 341 Python-derived reference files, including 35 XLSX/XLSM
files. Native vectors compare normalized fields, fingerprints and previews.
Hybrid cases compare complete typed book dumps and assert Rust routing for
every import and preview. Raw CLI bytes and full typed dumps, including failed
imports and rollback, are compared on SQLite and SQLCipher. Coordinator cases
cover supplied-map persistence, scoped dedupe, repeated prices, changed prices,
invalid later rows, missing scopes and late batch-link failures on both codecs.
The bulk matrix uses a synthetic SQLCipher raw key to avoid repeating key
derivation for every fixture. Coordinator wire checks retain ordinary
passphrases.

The following Python reference quirks are intentionally retained:

- Sats-denominated inferred columns multiply unit prices by the original sats
  count before converting the Bitcoin amount, inflating the resulting value.
- A preamble before the header can make a file unrecognized even when the
  workbook sheet picker found that header.
- Empty previews report `amount_max` as `0.000000`.
- A native `1 LBTC` amount cell refuses because the shared suffix reader strips
  the shorter BTC suffix first.
- Reimporting an unchanged priced row invalidates journals again.

Run `uv run --locked python -m tests.rust_port.repro_ledger_reference` offline
for all five reproductions. Python production code is unchanged. The
[shared CSV refusal](#shared-csv-reference-refusal) applies through the shared
reader.

## Privacy hygiene checkpoint (R5 reports privacy, partial)

this base; the year-handoff checkpoint above supplies the acceptance standard.

The service reads the active database header, configured endpoint/provider
posture, watch-only material counts, transaction/inventory aggregates and stored
journal freshness. Output remains count-only and redacted. It never probes a
provider or endpoint, launches an external process, refreshes observations or
journals, or changes custody/accounting authority. The report is available even
when journals need processing, matching Python's informational-read boundary.

route or `kassiber-net` grant is needed. The process oracle arms the strict
attempt observer for both implementations, including loopback.

and after the read. The seed retains Python's immutable compatibility audit

classification, Python 3.11 private-range exceptions, transport/proxy/owner
precedence, provider acknowledgement and truthiness, watch-only configuration,
freshness, malformed markers, count-column failures and raw JSON placeholders.

## Lightning profitability preparation checkpoint (R5, incomplete)

`t3code/r5-reports-lightning` starts at `9338364db`, the cross-check checkpoint.
The new `kassiber_reports::lightning` module prepares profitability payloads,
CSV rows and CSV files from an already curated routing/open-channel projection.
It also implements profile-scoped connection lookup and the daemon's window
coercion. The report-specific types have no node-pubkey, backend credential,
invoice, payment, forward-event or route fields. The module does not fetch a
snapshot, infer ownership, rebuild journals, calculate tax, acquire prices,
persist node data or change report-readiness barriers. There is no new egress.

This is an **unregistered preparation boundary**, not completion of the live
Lightning read/export family. Python's CLI and desktop profitability reads,

checkpoint. Registering a report renderer alone would advertise an incomplete
route. No CLI or daemon registry entry is added, and AI projections stay Python.

The report preserves the snapshot's summary values, including its authoritative
net, and keeps channel order and the inclusive covers-open-cost comparison.
Missing routing becomes the reference zero summary and label; missing channel
earnings become zero. Report quantities use unbounded integer sat, as Python's
profitability API does. CSV BTC text preserves Python's correctly rounded
int/int-to-binary64 division and fixed eight-place formatting; this float is
never an accounting input. The explicit operator CSV retains Python's channel
alias and ID columns. It contains no node pubkey, invoice/payment fields or
backend configuration. This full projection must not be exposed as an AI tool
or repurposed as a shareable diagnostics export.

Publication retains direct open/truncate, literal paths, CRLF, quoting, errors
and partial writes. It creates no parent directories, saved report marker,
dependency capture or filed marker. The tested reference quirks are retained:

- Large exact sat integers can lose visible precision in the CSV BTC column;
  sat text and JSON integers remain exact.
- A supplied net need not equal the separately rounded summary totals, and
  an absent routing window silently reports zeros while retaining channel rows.
- A surrogate in a CSV field raises an encoding error after truncation and
  can leave header/summary rows in the destination.
- Deep wallet-config nesting escapes the recoverable malformed-config path
  as `RecursionError`; an infinite daemon window escapes as `OverflowError`.

`t3code/r5-reports-lightning-2` starts at `35754114f`. This continuation adds

The client reads Python's nine fixed REST resources in order and resolves
missing private-peer aliases in sorted, deduplicated order, including peers

does not invent pagination, rebalance attribution or on-chain cost allocation.

between payment seconds/nanoseconds. Summary routing revenue floors the sum of
msat, while per-channel revenue and payment costs floor each event separately.

forward events, routes or raw failures. Private peer ids are request-local
alias lookup inputs, with the neutral `private peer` fallback. The client
performs no database write, journal refresh, ownership decision, tax
calculation, price acquisition or readiness change. Existing AI tools stay on
their Python redacted path.

returning a completed projection. Native CLN is covered by `KASSIBER_NO_EGRESS`,
unlike Python's CLN path. The child still owns its RPC/commando transport; the
parent does not claim to enforce or observe child DNS, proxy or TLS. RAM
metadata is a closed process marker with no command, credential or response.
The test observer blocks all unapproved subprocesses, even in loopback mode;

reviewed document core. Nothing is selected by default; confidence-only rows
require the explicit override, and malformed financial facts remain blocked.

input, EOF and an interrupted reader cancel without a write.

against the current Python implementation. This checkpoint does not register

## Source-funds case-save checkpoint (R5 partial)

The next `t3code/r5-sof-mutations-4` boundary composes the landed native report

The save dispatch precedes the report read savepoint. Ordinary saves acquire

truncated scope before composing the frozen report with SVGs. The fingerprint
binds the canonical recipe, report, reachable authored records, attachment
metadata/hashes and journal input version; derived bulk eligibility remains
outside it. The new native `ui.source_funds.review_context` uses the same
producer and deterministic flow ordering as saving. The read-only producer
still explicitly refuses direct saving without writer admission. Caller-owned
transactions remain untouched when reviewed admission refuses them.

## Corrupt-marker daemon diagnostics (R5 privacy continuation)

The configuration-hygiene daemon preserves Python's unhandled diagnostic field
under plan 21's native runtime exception. An `internal_error` from
`ui.reports.privacy_hygiene` returns `error.debug: ""`, an honest zero-frame native
diagnostic. Python emits a sanitized traceback string for this unhandled daemon
failure with or without global `--debug`, so Rust preserves a string in both
modes. Typed refusals retain `debug: null`. This conversion does not change
other daemon kinds or the existing CLI debug contract.

The native helper reuses the ordered, redacted ordinary error envelope and
changes only its existing debug value. It emits no stderr traceback, native
frame paths or locals, and invents no Python frames. The request loop rolls
back before returning the error and continues serving subsequent requests.

## PSBT parser prerequisite (R5 privacy PSBT, partial)

`t3code/r5-privacy-psbt` starts at `3291f143a`. The native
`kassiber-wallets::psbt` now provides the shared v0/v2 decoder, the transient

The parallel Mirror worker owns the shared observation/linkage prerequisites.

Binary, Base64 and hex inputs share the decoded-byte commitment. Text whitespace
and Base64 padding follow Python. Parsing bounds decoded payloads to 2 MiB,
text to three times that many characters, byte-encoded text to three times that
many bytes, unsigned transaction legs to 4,096, and individual maps to 10,000 entries.
Borrowed map slices and checked offsets avoid allocations from attacker-chosen
lengths. Embedded transaction and witness loops consume bytes or refuse.
Unknown and proprietary map contents exist only during the call.

The decoder preserves canonical framing, singleton/version restrictions,
construction-stage zero-input v0 transactions, explicit zero sequences, BIP370
required-locktime compatibility/maximum resolution, duplicate-outpoint refusals,
monetary limits, non-witness transaction hashes, prevout indices and supplied
amount/script consistency. It validates supplied redeem/witness script bindings,
public-key/derivation encodings and partial-signature encodings/sighash agreement.
Existing workspace Bitcoin consensus parsing and hashing validate non-witness
UTXOs; no dependency, lockfile or schema changes are introduced.

The existing public-feature extractor/rules consume a transient categorical
adapter. Analysis exposes amounts, evidence categories and metadata-presence
flags, without scripts, keys, xpubs, derivations, stacks or proprietary values.
Final vsize requires every input's supplied final stack; exact rates use the
application's 32-digit decimal context. Supplied UTXOs remain unverified for
chain membership and unspentness. Signatures are encoding observations only.
`decode_structure` deliberately returns scripts for the local inventory matcher;
that internal result must never enter storage or AI disclosure. This module has
no connection, endpoint, file-path, signing, finalizing or broadcasting API.

## Mirror process and book-bound handles (R5, partial)

`analysis_index::handles` adds opaque HMAC-SHA256 references to a bounded
32,768-entry RAM registry. A process-local key comes from SQLite's read-only
random generator. References bind the database location, profile and existing
database-instance identity. Successful replay refreshes LRU recency; eviction,
unissued references, another scope, another process and a fresh registry refuse
with the existing retryable stale-reference error. Keys are cleared on drop.

Only nested `subject` and `target` inputs are decoded. The public decoder derives
its book scope from the borrowed SQL view and revalidates each subject against
that current view. The caller cannot substitute a different scope. No handle
registry or key is persisted, and generic AI projections remain Python.

| Dataset expiry | 57 |
| Verified-tip generation | 6 |
| Watermark-only update | 6 |
| Missing table and trigger repair | 171 |
| Incremental output/spender change | 97 |
| Warm retained generation | 5 |
| Explicit rebuild | 95 |

`t3code/r5-chain-analysis-reads-2` continues the
[local read checkpoint](#chain-analysis-local-read-checkpoint-r5-partial) at
`00636290f`. It cherry-picks the native PSBT parser `fff419a68` as `76f39a6e5`.
The four remaining CLI leaves are `chain-analysis psbt analyze`,
`psbt compare`, `psbt entropy` and `datasets preview`. The daemon adds
`ui.chain_analysis.psbt.analyze`, `.psbt.compare`, `.psbt.entropy`,
`.datasets.preview`, `.entropy.start`, `.psbt.entropy.start`,
`.datasets.preview.start`, `.jobs.get` and `.jobs.cancel`. It also adds
`internal.chain_analysis.stage`, which issues the source tokens these kinds
consume. Every requested Chain Analysis read is now served natively. AI
projections stay in Python. Registry additions are appended after the earlier
read kinds.

`kassiber-wallets::psbt` gains proposal comparison and explicit BIP78 checks.
These include BIP143 commitments for the six supported sighash types, verified
with libsecp256k1. Public-key encodings follow embit's refusals: no hybrid keys,
and high-S signatures fail. Redacted analysis keeps Python's dict insertion
order, including the different field order of PSBT-adapter signature rows.
`analysis_index::runtime` holds the daemon's receipts and grants, under the
reference limits:

- Receipts: 16 retained, 2 concurrent, a one-hour lifetime, busy refusals and
  the start/get/cancel receipt shape.
- Grants: 32 retained for 30 minutes. Each is pinned to a book, a purpose and
  the selected file's device, inode, size and timestamps. Every read re-checks
  that identity.
- Previews: completed results are remembered for later import consent.

Receipt IDs and tokens come from SQLite's OS-seeded `randomblob`. Workers never
hold the caller's connection. `daemon.lock`, a successful `ui.profiles.switch`,
restore close and shutdown clear grants and receipts. Restore first quiesces
workers for up to five seconds, as `JOBS.quiesce` does.

`reads::preview` streams `utf-8-sig` records bounded to 64 KiB and the 8 GiB
input limit. It ports CPython 3.11's strict excel CSV reader state machine and
DictReader shape checks. It also ports JSONL row bounds, Maru92/generic claim
mapping, manifest and claim text/date/window rules, and `urlsplit`'s
credential/query/fragment, bracketed-host and NFKC delimiter refusals (the
Unicode 14.0 table). Lone surrogates in a subject are now refused as invalid
subjects in the shared `canonical_subject`, matching Python's `_text` acceptance
followed by a parse failure.

Python's `normalize_manifest` iterates a `set`, so the manifest field order, and
which of several invalid required fields is reported, follow `PYTHONHASHSEED`.
The native port uses sorted order. `tests/rust_port/repro_dataset_manifest_hashseed.py`
records eight seeds in
`crates/wallets/tests/data/chain_analysis_dataset_manifest_hashseeds.json`: eight
key orders, three first-error variants and one canonical value. Python is not
changed. The oracles pin the reference's set to sorted order, and process tests
reorder only the reference's manifest objects before comparing bytes.

Unchanged-Python oracles compare unsorted compact envelope bytes, schema and all
112 table commitments, and transaction state:

- PSBT: 254 cases, covering text, hex, binary and file payloads, all BIP vectors,
  validation order, entropy limits and scenarios, and 37 Payjoin constraint
  cases. Another 52 signed receiver proposals cover p2wpkh and p2sh-p2wpkh under
  every sighash, with corrupted, high-S, hybrid-key, missing-witness and
  fee-contribution cases.
- Dataset preview: 207 cases, covering manifests, 34 source URLs, CSV quoting,
  newlines, BOM, limits, NUL and UTF-8 errors, JSONL bounds, duplicate and
  surrogate keys, NaN values, Maru92 and am-i-exposed adapters, and Liquid
  addresses.

Whole-process CLI and daemon runs use strict no-consent guards with product
offline mode off and on; no configured provider, DNS, HTTP, RPC, socket or
loopback probe runs. Daemon transcripts mask only receipt IDs, elapsed time,
request IDs, the first receipt's completion race and a cancellation race.

| CLI leaf (`chain-analysis.` prefix) | Rust | Python |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `psbt.analyze` | 16 | 0 |
| `psbt.compare` | 10 | 0 |
| `psbt.entropy` | 8 | 0 |
| `datasets.preview` | 24 | 0 |

Four native daemon sessions compare 44 PSBT/receipt responses and 29
preview/receipt responses each, with zero Python fallback. The responses cover
staging, token reuse across purposes, changed files, failed and completed
workers, and lock fencing.

Known boundaries: Python's JSONL recursion cutoff depends on the caller's stack
depth, while native parsing stops at 1,000 nested containers. Bracketed IPv6
hosts use Rust's address parser. Non-UTF-8 staged file names are reported
lossily. Non-Unix grants pin size and modification time only. None of these
widens authority or egress.

Named mutations live in `chain_analysis_psbt_reads_mutations.json` (14) and
`chain_analysis_dataset_preview_mutations.json` (14). All 28 compile in scratch
trees and are killed by their named tests. The doubled-quote CSV recipe first
survived because no case showed a literal quote. It was killed on rerun after
the `csv-doubled-quote` case was added.

Local verification on Linux passes:

- all 52 native analysis-index tests, including 15 read, PSBT, preview and
  runtime tests;
- 64 daemon, CLI and runtime crate tests;
- 40 Python/native checks across the read, PSBT, preview, PSBT-primitive and
  inherited dataset/source/analytics oracles, without skips;
- workspace formatting, and Clippy for the affected crates with warnings denied;
- the required classifier update (5,775 definitions) and CI preflight (57 tests).

Toolchains were Rust 1.99.1, locked Python 3.11.17 and offline Cargo. Account
`HOME` was preserved. Evidence stays under `target/r5-reads-2/`; scratch
mutation trees are removed. There are no dependency or lockfile changes. The
full workspace suite, the Python/frontend quality gate and packaged/platform
