- An egressing read (`ui.reports.lightning_profitability`,
  `ui.connections.node.snapshot`) runs only with a consent bound to its call id
  (`consented_call_ids`) and otherwise answers `consent_required` without
  touching the book. Python leaves this to the chat loop. Both tools are refused
  after consent too, because their routes are not native.
- Rust's `test.ai_tool` opens a plaintext book lazily, as the daemon does. The
  reference wrapper opens it the same way before calling Python's executor.

**Python quirks kept.**

- Journal refresh is decided by the name as called. Models use wire names, so
  only the planner's dotted auto-reads ever refresh
  (`tests/rust_port/repro_ai_refresh_wire_name.py`).
- Design §7 item 10 (trailing-newline patterns, key-substring blanking,
  ASCII-escaped length limits) and item 12 (unredacted consent summaries).

**Read tools still refused.** 23 of the 100 read tools answer
`not_implemented` before the book is touched, because their services or
AI-only pieces are not native:

- `ui.overview.snapshot`, `ui.workspace.health`, `ui.next_actions`,
  `ui.report.blockers` and `ui.workspace.overview.snapshot` (workspace overview,
  health and readiness);
- `ui.journals.snapshot`, `.quarantine`, `.events.list` and `.transfers.list`;
- `ui.review.cases`, `.request_input`, `.plan`, `ui.review.badges` and the
  `ui.review.worklist` composite;
- `ui.transactions.graph` and the `ui.transactions.review_context` composite;
- `ui.audit.evidence.summary`;
- `ui.wallets.identify` and `ui.wallets.analyze_file`;
- `ui.reports.privacy_mirror` and the egress-ledger `ui.egress.snapshot`;
- `ui.reports.lightning_profitability` (its aggregate-only projection) and
  `ui.connections.node.snapshot` (the node route).

The other 77 run natively. They include the 25 chain-analysis reads, which the
design doc's §2 still listed as not native.

**Evidence.**

- **Python vectors.** `crates/ai/tests/python_vectors.rs` replays Python's
  answers (`scripts/gen_vectors.py`, stable across `PYTHONHASHSEED`s 0, 1 and
  12345) for capabilities, 710 selection cases, about 10,000 catalog-schema
  validations plus synthetic schemas, redaction, consent summaries, call
  parsing, the planner, context trimming at its exact limits, provenance and
  the chain-analysis projection.
- **Fences.** `crates/ai/tests/fences.rs` pins each privacy fence:
  - only advertised tools run;
  - egressing reads need bound consent;
  - auto-reads skip egressing tools;
  - once-only grants are never remembered;
  - results are redacted before they leave;
  - custody reads need a local provider, and on-device-only tools are neither
    offered to nor run for other providers;
  - there is no shell, filesystem, descriptor, secret or configuration tool;
  - skill references come only from the allowlist.
- **Executor parity.** `tests/test_rust_ai_tools.py` runs every read tool
  through Python's `_execute_read_only_ai_tool` (via
  `tests/rust_ai_tool_reference.py`) and through `test.ai_tool`. It covers each
  argument case and executor state (remote, local, MCP-like, not advertised,
  stale book and stale project) on separate copies of three fixture books
  (empty, desktop, reports). About 240 records per book compare byte for byte,
  envelope and model-visible bytes alike. Auto-read streams match on two books,
  and a `ca-ref:` handle round trip resolves the same subject in both. The
  declared mappings are `generated_at` clocks and per-session renaming of
  `ca-ref:` handles and chain-analysis snapshot digests.
- **No network traffic.** Every run uses `KASSIBER_TEST_NO_EGRESS=strict`, and
  the whole Rust session repeats unchanged inside an empty network namespace
  (`unshare --map-current-user --net`). The `kassiber-net` chokepoint scanner
  covers the new crate, and its dependency edge is reviewed.
- **Mutations.** `crates/ai/scripts/mutations.json`: 22 entries, all killed by
  named tests.

**Found outside this slice.** The native chain-analysis `snapshot_id` differs
from Python's and between two Rust runs on the same book; it is stable within
one session. The driver maps it like a handle. The native chain-analysis owner
should make it deterministic. (Resolved in
[R6-5b](#ai-tool-writes-previews-and-projections-r6-5b): the derivation was
already Python's; two read paths drew the index identity from the wrong
source.)

**Left for R6-5b.**

- **Executor and previews.** The mutating executor (59 + 2 tools) with the
  custody AI audit writer, and the consent previews (review apply, acquisition
  and dataset previews).
- **Projections.** The review worklist and transaction review composites, the
  `ui.chain_analysis.ai_context` kind, the remaining `_for_ai` builders
  (Lightning profitability, node snapshot, file analysis) and the
  `ui.review.receipt` kind-override receipts end to end.
- **AI-path parameters.** Metadata edits with `ai_tool`, `ui.wallets.sync` with
  `strict=True, auto_pair_journals=False`, and the `ui.review.*` workflow.
- **Chat dependencies.** Duplicate call ids and the chat-loop consent records
  belong to R6-7.

## AI providers, HTTP streaming and discovery (R6-6a)

`t3code/r6-6a-providers` starts at `6297511d1`, the first commit of R6-5a,
which created `crates/ai`. It ports the R6-6a scope of the
[R6 design](r6-ai-operator-port.md#r6-6-providers-http-streaming-broker-client-and-discovery).
No dependency, schema or Python product file changes.

| Surface | Native | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai.providers.list`, `.get`, `.create`, `.update`, `.set_api_key`, `.move_api_key`, `.delete`, `.set_default`, `.clear_default`, `.acknowledge` | yes | contact nothing; the desktop keychain only through `supervisor.ai_secret_store.*` |
| `ai.provider_runtime.status` | display reads | `cached_only` and "nothing a row allows" never probe; a runtime probe answers `not_implemented` (broker, R6-6b) |
| `ai.list_models` | HTTP rows | probes on a cold or expired cache, or on `refresh`; CLI rows answer `not_implemented` |
| `ai.test_connection` | HTTP targets | one `GET /models`, at most three `POST`s per format; CLI locators answer `not_implemented` after every validation |
| `ai providers list`/`get`/`create`/`update`/`delete`/`set-default`/`clear-default` | yes | `--api-key-fd`, `--api-key-stdin`, or the argv shim with Python's warning |
| `ai providers test`, `ai models` | HTTP rows | as the daemon kinds; CLI rows answer `not_implemented` |

**Crates.** `crates/ai` gains `providers` (`kassiber/ai/providers.py`), the
`transport` client (`client.py`), `discovery` (`discovery_cache.py`,
`model_metadata.py`) and `service`, which serves both surfaces. Document OCR
in `crates/wallets` now resolves, gates and maps errors through the same
store, so chat, discovery and OCR cannot disagree about a provider.
`kassiber-net` gains `HttpRequest::open`, a streaming reader that decodes
`Content-Length`, chunked and close-delimited bodies incrementally with every
framing byte charged against the limit and a bounded line reader, and a
`Cancel` handle that shuts the in-flight socket down from another thread.
`send` keeps its behaviour and shares the redirect loop. The daemon keeps one
RAM-only discovery cache for its lifetime, invalidated by every provider edit
except the preference-only ones Python exempts.

**Transport.** Responses and Chat Completions bodies are built in Python's key
order and written with `json.dumps` defaults. The SSE splitter keeps Python's
quirks: only `\n` ends a line, all leading spaces of `data:` go, trailing CRs
are stripped, only the exact `[DONE]` ends the stream. Both stream parsers,
the tool-call accumulators (Responses slots by output index and ids; Chat
Completions strictly by index, failing closed on a reused id), OpenRouter's
reasoning details, the auto fallback (once, on a missing route, before
anything answered), the relaxations (each part at most once; `store: false`
never), the error mapping and the connection test follow `client.py`.

**Reviewed differences.**

- A streamed or buffered provider response is capped at 64 MiB and one SSE
  line at 16 MiB (design §7, item 4, recommendation followed; Python reads
  without a bound). Over the cap is `ai_unavailable`.
- Transport failures carry `kassiber-net`'s fixed reason text
  (`network I/O failed`) instead of the OS error string, and an invalid HTTP
  message or a redirect loop is `ai_unavailable`. Python lets `IncompleteRead`
  and `BadStatusLine` escape as unhandled exceptions and maps a redirect loop to
  the last 3xx status.
- A cancelled request refuses before connecting, or shuts its socket down;
  the turn then ends quietly with what arrived, as Python's closed response does.

**Privacy fences.** Listing, reading and editing providers contacts nothing:
the service tests run them with a host whose gate panics, and the parity
driver's CRUD session leaves the scripted provider untouched. Contact happens
only from `ai.list_models`, `ai.test_connection`, `ai providers test` and
`ai models`, after the enabled, acknowledgement and endpoint gates, through a
route authorized for that request. Offline mode refuses everything but a
provider marked local on a loopback URL, with Python's message; a remote row
on `localhost` is refused. `KASSIBER_NO_EGRESS` leaves AI alone, as in Python
(the parity driver runs with it set). Keys reach only the `Authorization`
header: never argv (beyond Python's deprecated shim, with its warning),
envelopes, the egress ledger or logs. Error bodies use the 512-character
redacted preview.

**Evidence.** `cargo test -p kassiber-ai` (providers, transport, discovery,
service units, and `tests/http_transport.rs`: 33 ports of
`test_ai_core_http_transport.py`, `AutoFallbackTest` and the client classes
of `test_ai_core.py` against `kassiber_net::test_support::ScriptedProvider`).
`tests/test_rust_ai_providers.py` runs Python (`tests/rust_port/ai_providers_reference.py`,
clocks pinned by `KASSIBER_RUST_TEST_AI_TIME` and `KASSIBER_RUST_TEST_AI_CHECKED_AT`)
and the test-harness binary on copies of one book: 44-request CRUD, model
listing, connection-test and offline daemon sessions answer byte for byte,
the provider tables end identical (the secret ref `service` is compared as
"this root's"), the scripted provider sees identical requests, and 15 CLI
calls through the hybrid candidate are all served by Rust. With
`KASSIBER_TEST_CLI` naming the hybrid candidate, the boundary-fixture classes
`ProviderTestCliTest`, `ProviderFormatCliTest`, `ProviderSettingsCliTest`,
`ProviderKindInferenceCliTest` and `ProviderDisabledCliTest` pass 6 of 8
tests with all 18 `ai` calls served by Rust. The other two
(`test_store_field_flags`, `test_enable_disable_and_default_effort_flags`)
hit their 60 s and 120 s subprocess timeouts creating a fresh book while the
shared build disk sat at about 80% I/O pressure (one commit took seconds;
`status` on a fresh book took 63 s); they need a rerun on an idle disk.
`crates/ai/scripts/mutations.json` holds 19 entries (route phrases, single
relaxation, status mapping, same-origin redirects, acknowledgement and
test-target gates, kind inference, TTL, three SSE quirks, the store regex and
invariant, fallback, offline loopback, key origin, secret namespace,
duplicate call ids, cut-off calls), each killed by named tests.

**Remaining for R6-6b** (done; see the
[R6-6b checkpoint](#ai-provider-broker-client-r6-6b)). The provider broker
client (`broker_client.py`) and its gated process route: Node spawn in a new process group with the
`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` temp-root checks, the JSONL exchange with keep-alive and
per-leg watchdogs, TERM-then-KILL, the three environment overrides, and the
attempt observer. With it, `ai.provider_runtime.status` probes,
`ai.list_models`/`ai models` and connection tests on CLI rows (including
`binary_presence` check kinds) stop answering `not_implemented`.

## AI provider broker client (R6-6b)

`t3code/r6-6b-broker-client` starts at `40caf2ea2`, the R6-6a tip. It ports
the R6-6b scope of the
[R6 design](r6-ai-operator-port.md#r6-6-providers-http-streaming-broker-client-and-discovery).
No schema or Python product file changes, and no new crate in the lockfile.

| Surface | Native | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai.provider_runtime.status` | yes | `cached_only` and "nothing a row allows" still never probe; otherwise one broker `status` request for the allowed runtimes, or only the named row's runtime |
| `ai.list_models`, `ai models` | yes | CLI rows ask the broker for `models` (35 s cap) |
| `ai.test_connection`, `ai providers test` | yes | CLI targets list models through the broker (10 s); the probe is skipped (`cli_provider`), `check_kind` is `binary_presence` when a row says so |

**Crates.** `kassiber-net` gains the broker process route
(`Request::ai_broker`, `Route::spawn_broker`, `Subsystem::Ai`,
`Operation::Process`): the program lookup (`KASSIBER_AI_BROKER_NODE`, `node`
on `PATH` as Python 3.11's `shutil.which` finds it, the fixed fallbacks;
`KASSIBER_AI_PROVIDER_BROKER`), the `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` temp-root checks, the
private `kassiber-ai-broker-*` root (mode 0700) passed as
`KASSIBER_AI_BROKER_TMPDIR`, a new process group on Unix, and a signal handle
for SIGTERM, SIGKILL and waiting from any thread. It now uses `nix` (already
in the lockfile for `kassiber-paths`) for `killpg`, `getuid` and
`access(X_OK)`, with the new `signal` feature reviewed; it still forbids
`unsafe`. `crates/ai` gains `broker`, the client (`BrokerAIClient`):
`runtime_status`, `single_result` and `BrokerClient` with `list_models`,
`stream_chat` and a cancel handle. `ai.chat` is R6-7; the client's chat legs
are proven by the stream driver below.

**Protocol.** Requests are written with `json.dumps` defaults in Python's key
order; tool-call arguments with sorted keys and compact separators. A probe
writes one line, closes stdin, and must reach EOF and exit within its
deadline (35 s for status); on overrun the group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
after two seconds, and the request is `ai_unavailable`. Its output is read as
Python's text pipe (`\r\n` and `\r` become `\n`) and split with
`str.splitlines()`, so a raw U+2028 breaks a line there as in Python, while
chat legs split on `\n` only, as Python's line iterator does. A chat leg has
its own watchdog (`max(timeout, 1 s)`) that kills the group; after a
`tool_call` the process stays alive for `tool_results`, which must answer
every pending call. Each leg rechecks the online gate (Python calls
`require_online` on every leg), and so does every write. A finished process
gets SIGTERM, SIGKILL after two seconds, then a group SIGKILL for stragglers
before its root is removed. Error events map as `_broker_event_error`; a
private turn hides the provider's text.

**Reviewed differences.**

- Broker output Python cannot decode (not UTF-8, a line over 16 MiB, a probe
  over 64 MiB, an integer over 4,300 digits, nesting past 1,000) is
  `ai_unavailable` "The local AI provider broker returned invalid output".
  Python reads without a bound and lets the decode error escape.
- The broker leads a new process group (`process_group(0)`), not a new
  session: `setsid` needs an `unsafe` `pre_exec`. Signals reach the same
  group; a CLI started from a terminal keeps that controlling terminal.
- Without an override the script is `<executable dir>/provider_broker/index.mjs`
  (design §7 item 8, settled with R7 packaging). `~user` in an override is
  expanded on Unix only; Windows expands `~` alone.
- After a probe overruns, Rust waits for the broker to exit but not for EOF:
  a grandchild that left the group cannot pin the request.
- An unexpected pipe failure that Python lets escape becomes `internal_error`
  with Python's `[Errno N] reason` text.
- Dropping a client ends a broker it kept alive for tool results.

**Privacy fences.** No broker starts without the online gate and an
explicit-trigger consent bound to the program: offline mode (or an unreadable
preference) refuses every probe, listing and chat leg with Python's message
and no attempt, and a tool session refuses its next leg once offline mode is
on. Every launch goes through `Route::spawn_broker`, where an armed observer
records it (`scheme` `broker`, port 1); a strict observer, or a script other
than the one a harness named (`KASSIBER_RUST_TEST_AI_BROKER_FIXTURE` in
test-harness builds), trips the guard before anything starts. The product
ledger records no launch, as Python records none (design §7 item 3).
`KASSIBER_NO_EGRESS` leaves the broker alone, as in Python. The broker's argv
is `[node, script]`; no key reaches it, and requests carry no credentials.
Nothing runs at launch, on idle, on provider listing or editing, on
`cached_only` status, or when no row allows a runtime: the parity driver's
CRUD session leaves the fake broker's log empty, and an empty runtime list
starts nothing. A missing Node or script starts nothing and counts no
attempt. Windows code paths (`TerminateProcess` instead of group signals,
`USERPROFILE` home expansion, `PATHEXT` lookup, the private-turn refusal) are
written to compile but were not built here; review them on Windows.

**Evidence.** `cargo test -p kassiber-net` (12 broker units, including
`BrokerTempParentTest`'s 7) and `cargo test -p kassiber-ai`
(`tests/broker.rs`: 30 tests porting `BrokerClientTest` and the broker classes
of `test_ai_fast_mode.py` against the same fake brokers, plus the fences;
`tests/broker_windows.rs` for Windows; the service unit test now probes,
lists and tests a CLI row through a fake broker). `tests/test_rust_ai_providers.py`
adds daemon sessions for probes, cache reuse, listings, connection tests and
offline refusals, and CLI leaves through the hybrid candidate; envelopes,
tables and the fake broker's request lines match Python byte for byte, and
all `ai` calls are served by Rust. `tests/test_rust_ai_broker.py` drives
Python's `BrokerAIClient` (`tests/rust_port/ai_broker_reference.py`) and the
Rust client (`crates/ai/examples/broker_stream.rs`, named by
`KASSIBER_RUST_AI_BROKER_EXAMPLE`) through tool rounds, quirky output, error
events, invalid options, a mid-stream cancel and offline mode: every chunk,
leg outcome and broker request line matches. `crates/ai/scripts/mutations.json`
gains 17 R6-6b entries (launch observation, the fixture rule, the missing-program check, both temp-root checks, the straggler kill, the empty and filtered scopes, the cancel latch and signal, keep-alive, complete tool results, private cursors, explicit fast mode, known notices, the leg watchdog and `binary_presence`), all killed by named tests.
`test_provider_resume_cursor_is_bound_to_the_visible_chat_branch` tests the
daemon's chat registry and moves with R6-7.

## AI chat (R6-7)

`t3code/r6-7-chat` starts at `b12e22ac5`, the R6-6b tip, and merges
`322cfb0f0`, the R6-5a tip, so the read executor, the providers and the
broker client meet. It ports the R6-7 scope of the
[R6 design](r6-ai-operator-port.md#r6-7-chat). No schema, dependency or
Python product file changes; the lockfile is unchanged.

| Surface | Native | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai.chat` | behind the gate | worker thread per turn; book work runs as request-loop tasks |
| `ai.chat.cancel`, `ai.tool_call.consent` | behind the gate | answered before the book gate, from the RAM registry |
| `ui.chat.sessions.list`, `.get`, `.delete`, `.clear`, `ui.chat.history.configure` | behind the gate | the active profile's sessions; the stored policy |
| `chat` | behind the gate | re-executes the binary as `kassiber --data-root … --env-file … daemon` |
| `chats list`, `show`, `delete`, `clear`, `config` | behind the gate | on the open book |

**The gate.** Design §7 item 1 is followed: chat registers only when every
tool it can call is native. The `native-chat` cargo feature of
`kassiber-daemon` and `kassiber-cli` registers the eight kinds and six leaves;
only `kassiber`'s `test-harness` feature enables it, so product builds still
answer `not_implemented` and advertise none of them. The gate flips when:

- the mutating executor (R6-5b, 61 tools) runs natively, with the custody AI
  audit writer that records denied and cancelled custody proposals and the
  consent previews (`review_preview` for `ui.review.apply`, the acquisition
  and dataset previews);
- the 23 read tools R6-5a still refuses are native. The planner's automatic
  reads use `ui.workspace.health` and `ui.next_actions` for nearly every
  domain question, so a chat with the Kassiber prompt differs from Python
  until they are;
- document-import staging (`internal.document_import.stage` and its
  sessions) is native, for chat attachments and `kassiber chat --file`.

Flipping it means enabling `native-chat` in product builds (or dropping the
`cfg`) and moving `chat`/`chats.*` into `describe::IMPLEMENTED`.

**Crates.** `crates/ai` gains `prompt` (`kassiber/ai/prompt.py`; the Kassiber
system prompt is embedded from `src/data/catalog.json`, which
`scripts/gen_catalog.py` now also writes with the chat constants and the
screen-metric definitions) and `chat`:

- `args`: `_ai_chat_args` with the screen-context, metrics-scope, attachment
  and seed-notice checks, in Python's order;
- `registry`: `ActiveAiChats`, with early cancels held for 30 s (at most
  128) and provider cursors bound to the history fingerprint;
- `history`: `core/chat_history.py`, with uuid4 values from SQLite's
  `randomblob`;
- `screen`: the screen-context and attachment notes the model reads;
- `client`: the HTTP client or the broker behind one interface;
- `turn`: `_run_ai_chat_stream` and the tool loop;
- `store`: the book operations the storage layer serves (`Book::ai_chat`).

The HTTP client gains a per-turn `Receipt` (one record per request, with
Python's `http_request_bytes_out` estimate) and a `Revocation` that revokes
every consent the turn was granted. `kassiber-transactions` gains
`transaction_in_profile` and `bind_screen_metrics_scope`;
`Book::unlock_passphrase` hands `kassiber chat` the passphrase its daemon
child is unlocked with over stdin. `crates/daemon/src/ai_chat.rs` holds the
kinds and the worker host: an executor callback is served on the request loop
as a sequence of book calls over channels, so no closure crosses threads and
nothing needs `unsafe`. The loop polls every 50 ms while a worker runs, as
Python's does. `crates/cli/src/chat` ports `kassiber/cli/chat.py`,
`termrender.py` and `review_consent.py`; `crates/cli/src/chats.rs` the five
leaves.

**Record order.** `ai.chat.status` (preparing, connecting, waiting), then
deltas, `ai.chat.tool_call` (with the consent registered before the record),
`ai.chat.tool_consent_required`, `ai.chat.tool_result`, and one terminal
`ai.chat` or an error envelope. A cancel before registration, during the
stream, or while consent waits still ends with a terminal `cancelled`.

**Reviewed differences.**

- The privacy receipt counts the turn's own provider requests. Python counts
  every egress-ledger record after the turn's cursor, including unrelated
  daemon traffic in the same window; the Rust daemon has no process-wide
  product ledger yet (`ui.egress.snapshot` is not native), so `egress_gap` is
  always false. The broker records none, as in Python.
- A persisted exchange is one transaction. Python leaves a partial write in
  an open transaction when the final insert fails.
- Tools R6-5b owns: an allowed mutating call answers `not_implemented` after
  Python's gates; consent previews use plain argument redaction and the
  `ui.review.apply` record carries no `review_preview`, so the CLI denies it;
  denied or cancelled custody proposals write no audit row.
- An attachment grant is never known (staging is not native): `ai.chat`
  answers `document_import_session_expired` after resolving the book, as
  Python does for an expired grant, and `kassiber chat --file` fails on the
  staging kind.
- `kassiber chat` has no SIGINT handling (no signal API without a new
  dependency): Ctrl-C ends the session, and the daemon child stops at the end
  of its input instead of cancelling the turn cooperatively. It reads REPL
  lines without readline editing, sizes tool tables from `COLUMNS` only,
  kills a daemon child that outlives its input instead of sending SIGTERM
  first, and starts the child in the caller's working directory.

**Python quirks kept.** A provider session cursor is recorded against the
turn's transcript plus the last leg's answer and looked up against the next
request's whole transcript, so it is never resumed
(`tests/rust_port/repro_chat_cursor_never_resumes.py`). Design §7 item 11 is
taken as recommended: a provider row without a name is named "selected
provider" in the model hint.

**Privacy fences.** Nothing is contacted before the user's message: argument
validation, session lookup, provider resolution, screen binding and an early
cancel all run before any request (`an_early_cancel_contacts_nothing`, the
driver's validation and early-cancel scenarios). History is stored only for a
request that asked and only under the stored policy, where `auto` means an
encrypted book (`history_is_stored_only_under_the_policy`). The privacy
receipt counts what was sent (`the_privacy_receipt_counts_what_was_sent`).
Cancelling revokes the turn's network consent; a revoked consent refuses the
next request on its own (`cancelling_revokes_the_turns_network_consent`).
Offline mode refuses a remote provider and the broker before contact (driver).
On-device-only tools are never offered to other providers, only tools offered
this turn run, and a cut-off answer runs none of its calls.

**Evidence.**

- `cargo test -p kassiber-ai` adds the chat unit tests and `tests/chat.rs`
  (16 turn tests against the scripted provider, including the R6-6b handover
  `provider_resume_cursor_is_bound_to_the_visible_chat_branch` and
  `ChatHistorySeedTest`'s round trip).
- `tests/test_rust_ai_chat.py` (9 scenarios) runs one daemon session per side
  against the same scripted provider and fake broker and compares every
  record, grouped by request id, byte for byte after mapping uuid4 values;
  the chat, provider and settings tables; and every provider and broker
  request. It covers history and policy, 45 argument errors with no contact,
  the tool loop with consent, early cancel, cancel during consent, cancel
  after the book locks, the format fallback, a broker tool round with
  Incognito, and offline refusal.
- `tests/test_cli_chat.py` through the hybrid candidate: 39 of 41 pass with
  every `chat` and `chats` call served by Rust; the two daemon-session tests
  also pass with a Rust daemon. The two failures allow `ui.journals.process`
  and need R6-5b. Under heavy shared-disk load (test data on the 860 EVO,
  load average about 20) a rerun also hit the module's 15 s subprocess
  timeout on `init` and `ai providers create`; those tests pass alone.
- `tests/test_rust_ai_tools.py::AiCatalogDriftTest` now looks for the
  mutation entries' test names in all of `crates/ai` and `crates/net`, since
  the merged catalog names unit tests too, and the drift test
  `chat_constants_match_python` pins the chat constants and the embedded
  prompt to `catalog.json`. `tests/test_rust_hybrid_candidate.py` passes
  (35 tests, 4,741 subtests).
- The AI tests of `tests/test_daemon_smoke.py` with a Rust daemon: 70 of 75
  pass. Four need refused or mutating tools (R6-5b, the refused reads); one
  needs `ui.secrets.init`, which is not native.
- `crates/ai/scripts/mutations.json` gains 17 R6-7 entries (record order,
  consent before the record, the cancelled terminal, the auto policy, persist
  intent, the 16-iteration rule, the cross-book phrase, the receipt, both
  revocation halves, duplicate ids, cut-off answers, the advertised check,
  the on-device strip, held early cancels, their cap, cursor binding), all
  killed by named tests.

## MCP server and cooperative chat Ctrl-C (R6-8)

Slice R6-8 of the [R6 design](r6-ai-operator-port.md#r6-8-mcp-server).
`t3code/r6-8-mcp` starts at `12cad03e2` (the R6-7 tip) and merges
`8d3cbb7e6` (the R6-3 tip), so the read executor, chat and the operator
client meet. All six `mcp` leaves are native. Following design §7 item 1 as
R6-7 did for chat, `mcp serve` and `mcp call` register behind the
`native-mcp` cargo feature of `kassiber-cli`, which only `kassiber`'s
`test-harness` feature enables; `mcp tools`, `status`, `enable` and
`disable` need no tool and register in product builds. The gate flips when
the 13 MCP read tools R6-5a still refuses are native (`overview_snapshot`,
`workspace_health`, `next_actions`, `report_blockers`, `transactions_graph`,
`transactions_review_context`, the four `journals_*` reads, `review_cases`,
`review_plan`, `review_worklist`); until then they answer `not_implemented`
as the executor does. The slice also gives `kassiber chat` its cooperative
Ctrl-C, which R6-7 recorded as a difference. No dependency, schema or Python
product file changes.

### What is native

- **The protocol** (new crate `crates/mcp`, `kassiber/mcp/protocol.py`):
  both eras chosen per message (modern `_meta` revision 2026-07-28 with no
  session; legacy `initialize` for 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18, newest
  offered otherwise, `ping` before it), `server/discover`, `tools/list` and
  `tools/call` with Python's field order, `subscriptions/listen` with an
  empty filter, and every JSON-RPC error in Python's check order. The stdio
  loop answers other methods on the reader thread and runs calls one at a
  time on a worker; limits are 16 MiB per line (a longer line answers
  `Message too large` and is skipped), 32 calls in flight, 16 subscriptions;
  `notifications/cancelled` drops a call's reply (by id type: `1` and `"1"`
  differ); at end of input accepted calls get 30 s, then open streams get
  their final result. Replies are ASCII-escaped compact JSON. `NaN` and
  `Infinity` are parse errors (`kassiber_pytext::loads_py_without_constants`,
  Python's `parse_constant` hook); nesting past the scanner's limit is a
  parse error, not a crash.
- **The projection** (`kassiber/mcp/tools.py`): the 44 read tools in list
  order with names from the catalog's wire names, titles, schemas with
  `type: object`, the read-only annotations, `INSTRUCTIONS`, the 4 MiB
  result bound measured on the escaped text, and the redacted error outcome
  with its `code: message` / `hint:` text.
- **The leaves** (`crates/cli/src/mcp.rs`, `kassiber/mcp/cli.py`): `serve`,
  `tools`, `status`, `enable` and `disable` run before state migration,
  path resolution or broker routing, as Python's launch path does. `serve`
  refuses a half pin, then claims stdio (`kassiber_ipc::stdio::claim`:
  private duplicates of descriptors 0 and 1, then 0, 1 and 2 on
  `/dev/null`; `SetStdHandle` to `NUL` on Windows). `enable` asks on the
  user's terminal and refuses machine or piped callers with
  `interaction_required` (`reason: user_consent`). `mcp call` checks agent
  access and the book's existence before migration or routing, opens the
  book like any CLI read, and checks its pin and arguments after opening, in
  Python's order.
- **A call on a direct book** (`crates/daemon/src/mcp.rs`, `run_tool`): the
  access gate first, then `not_initialized` for a machine without projects
  or a selected project without a database (nothing is created); a
  plaintext or `unattended` book is bootstrapped, opened without prompting
  and accounted, the scope resolved, then pinned read-only for the call
  (`kassiber_store::pinned`: a temporary view shadows `settings` with the
  pinned context keys and `PRAGMA query_only` refuses writes; the stored
  context is never written), the R6-5a read executor runs as a remote
  provider with the 44 tools advertised, read maintenance off and no
  cross-book reads, and the result is redacted again and named by its book.
  The book closes after every call.
- **A call on a brokered book**: arguments are validated in this build
  first; `status` never starts a broker; without a lease the agent is told
  to ask the user (`operator_lease_required`); the pin or the lease's
  default scope names the book; an agent-scope lease registers this process
  as an agent session (10 s heartbeats, one session per book, a stale one
  replaced once by parallel callers, re-registered when the broker drops
  it); the call is submitted as `--machine mcp call` without starting a
  broker, only to this build's broker and only one that honours caller
  context; it is polled every 0.1 s, a cancelled call cancels its queued
  operation, and the child's envelope is mapped and redacted again.
- **Store seams**: `BookStore::runtime_paths`, `catalog_has_projects` and
  `agent_access_path`, and `Book::pin_read_only_scope`.
- **Chat Ctrl-C** (`crates/cli/src/chat`): once the daemon child starts,
  SIGINT is `crates/ipc`'s interrupt (new `take`, `wait_readable` and
  `exit_by_interrupt`). Mid-turn it sends `ai.chat.cancel` and waits for the
  terminal record, keeping the session; a second Ctrl-C there ends the turn
  with `cancelled`; at a consent question it cancels the turn; at the REPL
  prompt it ends the REPL; anywhere else the process ends by SIGINT after
  closing its daemon, as an uncaught `KeyboardInterrupt` does. Terminal reads
  wait for input or the interrupt, since the handler restarts system calls.
  The daemon child now leads its own process group, so the terminal's
  Ctrl-C reaches only the chat.

### Verification

- **Rust tests:**
  - `kassiber-mcp`: 28 protocol tests against a fake provider (the
    in-process `ProtocolEraTests`, `StdioLoopTests`,
    `SubscriptionLimitTests`, `StdioRobustnessTests` and the wire half of
    `StrictJsonTests`, with exact reply bytes, the error check order, id
    typing, the in-flight and subscription caps, the 16 MiB line limit
    around its boundary, a panicking provider and the bounded drain) and 7
    projection tests (names, titles, annotations, only local read tools,
    the escaped result bound at and past the limit, error texts).
  - `kassiber-cli`: 21 `mcp` tests over a scripted broker and a minimal
    store (`BrokeredRoutingTests`, `OutdatedBrokerMcpTests`, the broker half
    of `ReviewHardeningTests`, the access gates and their order, missing
    books, half pins and `--arguments`, `enable`/`disable`/`status`,
    `os.path.abspath`), and 6 chat tests for Ctrl-C over a scripted daemon
    (mid-turn cancel, the second Ctrl-C, a consent question, the prompt,
    the daemon wait, the child's own process group).
  - `kassiber-store`: the read-only pin on SQLite (`PinnedContextTests`).
  - `kassiber-ipc`: the interrupt taken once and its wait on a descriptor.
  - `kassiber-pytext`: `NaN`/`Infinity` refused, `1e999` still a float.
  - `crates/kassiber/tests/operator_broker.rs`:
    `mcp_serve_reads_a_brokered_book_once_the_desktop_allows_it` runs a Rust
    `mcp serve` against a Rust broker and daemon: a manual book asks for an
    unlock, the desktop's agent grant leaves the server pending until the
    user allows it (its pid shown), two reads run in broker children and are
    counted, and the desktop's lock returns the book to manual.
- **Python:**
  - `tests/test_rust_mcp.py` (13 tests): stdio transcripts of 14 messages that
    are not tool calls and 91 tool calls (80 argument cases over the 44
    tools, from the AI driver, plus 11 refusals) on the empty, desktop and reports fixture
    books, pinned and unpinned books, an unknown book, a missing data root,
    MCP off and the AI switch off, and a manual encrypted book: every reply
    identical to Python's byte for byte, except the reads R6-5a refuses
    (checked against that list). The one-shot leaves compare stdout and exit
    codes (10 `mcp call` variants, each with and without `--machine`, `tools`,
    `status`, `enable`, `disable`). The fences on Rust: launch and listing
    leave the home tree unchanged, create no data or state root, connect to
    no live operator endpoint and hold only `/dev/null` and two pipes; a
    direct read reaches no socket and closes its book; a brokered book with
    no broker answers `operator_lease_required` and no broker binds the
    runtime directory; only the 44 read tools answer. The mutation catalog
    applies and names existing tests.
  - `tests/test_rust_chat_interrupt.py` (3 tests): `kassiber chat` on a
    pseudo-terminal against a loopback provider holding its answer; a typed
    Ctrl-C cancels the turn (one request), keeps the session and its daemon
    (in its own process group), the next turn completes, a second Ctrl-C at
    the prompt exits 0, and a one-shot `--machine` chat returns
    `finish_reason: cancelled`.
  - `KASSIBER_TEST_OPERATOR_BROKER=rust` runs all six
    `test_operator_integration.py` scenarios, the MCP one unskipped: the
    Python provider's brokered reads run in Rust `mcp call` children, and
    the stranger is a Rust `mcp serve` (a fresh Python process names
    another build, which the Rust broker refuses before pairing). Python's
    broker passes them too, with `test_mcp_server.py` (62) unchanged.
  - `kassiber-net`'s chokepoint scanner passes with `kassiber-mcp` reviewed.
    It had failed since R6-7, whose chat child launch and `native-chat`
    feature forwarding were never added to the reviewed lists; both are now.
  - `tests/test_rust_ai_chat.py` and `tests/test_rust_operator_cli.py` pass
    on the merged branch; the operator daemon scenario failed once under a
    load average near 400 and passed alone.
- **Mutations.** `crates/mcp/scripts/mutations.json` has 38 entries, run by
  `crates/mcp/scripts/mutation_check.py` over `kassiber-mcp`,
  `kassiber-cli`, `kassiber-setup`, `kassiber-store` and `kassiber-ipc`:
  era selection (5), error codes (5), id typing (2), the in-flight,
  duplicate and subscription limits (3), cancellation and the drain (2),
  the escaped result size (2), the access gate's place and reason
  precedence (3), the brokered checks (never starting a broker, this build,
  caller context, re-redaction, one stale-session replacement, 0.1 s
  polling, cancelling queued work: 7), the pin (2) and chat Ctrl-C (7).
  All 38 are killed in scratch-tree runs. The first run left three
  survivors whose tests compared a constant with itself or did not reach
  the mutated line; those tests now pin Python's literal values.

### Reviewed differences

- Python's daemon child shares the chat's process group, so a terminal
  Ctrl-C kills it and the cooperative cancel then fails with
  `BrokenPipeError` (`tests/rust_port/repro_chat_ctrl_c_kills_daemon.py`,
  which also shows `close()` raising on the dead child). Rust starts the
  child in its own process group (`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows);
  the cancel works and the child exits at the end of its input.
- An uncaught Ctrl-C ends the process by SIGINT without Python's
  traceback on stderr.
- A Ctrl-C that lands between operations is handled at the next read
  (the REPL prompt, a consent question or a wait for the daemon); Python
  raises wherever it lands.
- The read-only pin is a temporary view rather than a Python context
  variable: a tool that wrote a context key would get SQLite's read-only
  error instead of `scope_pinned`. No read tool writes settings.
- The JSON nesting limit is the scanner's fixed 1,000 levels; Python's
  depends on its stack at the call.

### Not tested here

- Windows: the stdio claim through `SetStdHandle`, the chat child's
  `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` and terminal reads without the interrupt wait
  were written against `windows-sys` 0.61 and std, not compiled.
- macOS: the pseudo-terminal Ctrl-C test reads `/proc` and runs on Linux
  only.

### Left

- Turn the `native-mcp` gate on with the 13 refused read tools.
- `kassiber chat` line editing (R6-7's remaining difference).

## AI tool writes, previews and projections (R6-5b)

`t3code/r6-5b-ai-tools` merges R6-5a (`322cfb0f0`) into the r10b integration
tip `a0b4d0342` and finishes the executor side of
[R6-5](r6-ai-operator-port.md#r6-5-ai-tool-executor-catalog-and-projections).
Chat (R6-7) and MCP (R6-8) still drive nothing; the test-harness kinds
`test.ai_tool`, `test.ai_auto_read`, `test.ai_consent_preview` and
`test.ai_custody_record` run the executor, and stay out of release builds,
the desktop allowlists and every AI catalog.

**Read tools.** 99 of the 100 read tools run natively. Each refusal was lifted
only after the driver matched Python on the fixture books:

- overview, book-set overview, health and next actions; report blockers with
  the automatic refresh's failure applied, and `auto_report_blockers` after any
  other read whose refresh failed;
- journal snapshot, quarantine, events and transfers; review cases, input
  requests (stored with a redacted explanation), plans (refused when they would
  not fit a later apply call or carry private fields) and badges;
- the transaction graph, the transaction review composite and the review
  worklist (`crates/daemon/src/worklist.rs`), whose `safety` block reports
  whether the read prelude contacted the network;
- the evidence summary and file analysis of the chat's staged attachment
  (`core.file_analysis.redact_for_egress` for providers off the device);
- ownership identification (`redact_result_for_ai`; never a CSV harvest),
  the redacted Privacy Mirror, the AI egress view over the process ledger, and
  Lightning profitability reduced to its aggregate after a consent bound to
  the call.

`ui.connections.node.snapshot` still refuses: there is no native node-snapshot
route for its `snapshot_to_dict_for_ai` projection.

**Writes.** `kassiber_ai::mutate::execute_mutating` follows
`_execute_mutating_ai_tool`: argument errors, catalog and `kind_class`, the
local-provider custody gate, the advertised set, then (unlike Python, which
leaves it to the chat loop) a consent bound to the call id, then the schema and
the route. Every write runs on the request loop after the frozen project and
book check and reaches the native route the desktop uses; results are
redacted. The host (`crates/daemon/src/ai_tools.rs`) passes the AI-path
parameters:

- `ai_tool` authorship for metadata edits and reverts, quarantine resolutions
  (`Book::journal_view_as`), the review workflow (`review::execute_as`, with
  the operation authority checks of `_validate_ai_review_operations`) and the
  transfer and custody services;
- strict `ui.wallets.sync` arguments and a native plan executed with
  `auto_pair = false`; journal processing through `refresh_journals` without
  pairing; `ui.maintenance.run` skips an `if_enabled` refresh the turn already
  attempted (`settings::run_as`);
- export targets mapped as `_ai_report_export_target` maps them, saved locally
  and redacted.

Refused before the book: the `pdf` and audit-`package` targets of
`ui.reports.export` and `ui.source_funds.export` (renderers not native),
`ui.btcpay.provenance.review` (service not native), and `ui.wallets.sync` for
books whose sources the native freshness plan cannot take, which need
Python's direct-sync path. Every fixture book is such a book, so the driver
proves the strict arguments (Python vectors) and the refusal, not a native
sync; that path reuses the desktop route's plan and execution with pairing
off.

**Custody AI audit.** `kassiber_transfers::custody_ai_audit::append` ports
`append_assistance_record` (bounded proposals, facts and result digests).
`RealBook::custody_ai_write` runs a consented `ui.custody.review.apply` inside
`SAVEPOINT custody_ai_assisted_write` and commits it with its `executed` row;
a failure rolls back and commits a `failed` row with the error code.
`record_nonexecuted_custody_call` audits denied, timed-out and cancelled
custody proposals and nothing else.

**Consent cards.** `kassiber_ai::previews::consent_request` builds the
`ai.chat.tool_consent_required` data: summary, redacted arguments, and, in
place of the model's claims, the recomputed acquisition plan
(`acquire.apply`, `sources.authorize`), the remembered dataset validation
(`datasets.import`, `.start`; imports are refused unless they match it), and
the review preview (`review.validate` on the native workflow, or the applied
receipt for the same idempotency key). Previews write nothing authored.

**Projections and kinds.** The desktop kind `ui.chain_analysis.ai_context`
is native (`reads::ai_context` plus the `ca-ref:` projection).

**Fixes found by the driver.**

- The chain-analysis `snapshot_id` derivation already matched Python
  (`digest([instance_id, profile, VERSION, revision])` over a per-book
  `uuid4`). The instability came from two paths that drew the index identity
  from the wrong source: the Privacy Mirror used the report source and the
  chain-analysis reads used `SystemSources`; both now use the index's own
  analysis source. With `KASSIBER_RUST_TEST_ANALYSIS_IDS=sequential` both
  runtimes draw from one counter, and the driver compares snapshot ids byte
  for byte.
- Native journal view and quarantine freshness ignored calculation semantics,
  so books built under older semantics read as current with a shorter reason.

**Python reference bug, kept unfixed.** One wallet whose stored
configuration is not JSON makes Python's AI `ui.wallets.sync` fail as a
generic `tool_error` with a traceback, for the whole book
(`tests/rust_port/repro_ai_wallets_sync_bad_config.py`). Rust refuses such
books as needing the direct-sync path.

**Reviewed differences.**

- Writes, like egressing reads, run only with a consent bound to the call
  (`consented_call_ids`); Python leaves that to the chat loop.
- XLSX ZIP bytes differ between the writers, as in
  `tests/test_rust_full_xlsx.py`: the driver declares each side's artifact
  size and digest. Component-term and evidence-commitment digests hash their
  generated ids and map like the ids.

**Evidence.**

- `tests/test_rust_ai_tools.py`: every read tool (353 calls per book) and
  auto-read on three fixture books; every mutating tool's cases (schema fill,
  fixture rows, refusals; 189 calls per book) on separate copies per tool,
  comparing the whole envelope and model bytes per call and all 112 tables
  after the session, plus 12 Rust-only refusal checks per book that leave every
  table unchanged. Chain-analysis writes are compared mostly on their
  argument, scope and staleness refusals over the fixture books; their success
  paths are the native routes' own oracles (`tests/test_rust_analysis_ops.py`
  and its siblings); the custody
  writes, AI-authored writes and audit rows; consent cards for every
  consented tool, leaving authored tables unchanged; the review flow (plan,
  preview, apply, preview, receipt); kind-override receipts staying local end
  to end; `ui.chain_analysis.ai_context`; and the Rust run inside an empty
  network namespace. Declared mappings: generated ids and clocks, `ca-ref:`
  handles, and the XLSX and derived digests above.
- `crates/ai/tests/python_vectors.rs` adds Python's answers for the review
  operation rules, planned-artifact limits, export targets, strict sync
  arguments, sync failure detection, the egress view, file-analysis egress and
  ownership redaction.
- `crates/ai/tests/fences.rs` pins the write fences: consent bound to the call,
  advertised tools only, the local custody gate and audit record, the frozen
  book, refused exports, the dataset binding, redacted results, previews that
  never write, and composite reads that report their refresh.
- `crates/ai/scripts/mutations.json`: 47 entries (25 new, 6 of them process
  oracles), each killed by named tests.

**What chat still needs.** R6-7's duplicate call ids, consent records and
registration; and, before chat can match Python for every tool, the refusals
above (node snapshot, PDF and audit-package exports, commercial evidence
review, direct-sync wallet refresh).

## Text PDF reports (R5, partial)

## PDF reports (R5, partial)

The owner brought PDF into scope on 2026-11-02 and approved one shared report
design (`docs/reference/report-design.md`) on 2026-11-04; it replaces both
ReportLab's layouts and the hand-written fixed-pitch writer report by report.
`crates/pdf` holds the sealed Typst engine; `crates/reports/src/report_design`
builds every report's document from the model Python's writer receives.
Every CLI leaf below admits source freshness first, as Python's final-export
gate does, and every envelope inserts `pages` between `file` and `bytes`.

`reports export-summary-pdf` and
`ui.reports.export_summary_pdf` are native in that design: the model is
Python's `build_summary_pdf_report_data` (parity for 23 fixture cases), the
daemon kind admits only `start`, `end`, `wallets` and `include_snapshot` with
Python's messages, the managed name is `kassiber-summary-report-…pdf`, both
admit source freshness first and register the saved `summary.pdf` marker over
the period's years and wallets. The envelope keeps Python's keys and title;
`pages`, `bytes` and the content hash are the new PDF's.

`reports export-pdf` and `ui.reports.export_pdf` (the full report) are in the
shared design too, replacing the byte-ported text PDF: the model is Python's
`_build_full_report_context` read from the same stored inputs as the full CSV
(`full_pdf::model`, exact parity for 89 fixture cases, refusals included),
with the saved `full-report.pdf` marker as before.

`reports export-austrian-e1kv-pdf`, its alias `reports export-austrian` and
`ui.reports.export_austrian_e1kv_pdf` render the Austrian E 1kv report in the
design (German): the model is what Python's writer receives (E 1kv report,
portfolio, the tax year's transaction rows; parity for 47 fixture cases),
freshness admission first on the CLI, the saved `austrian-e1kv.pdf` marker
for the tax year, managed name `kassiber-austrian-e1kv-<year>-…pdf`. The
envelope keeps Python's keys; `renderer` is `typst`.

`reports export-exit-tax-pdf` and `ui.reports.export_exit_tax_pdf` render the
exit-tax estimate (`report_exit_tax`, parity in the exit-tax vectors) in the
design: German for Austrian books with Python's English notes translated by
their exact text, English otherwise; like Python, no saved marker.

Evidence: `tests/test_rust_pdf_exports.py` runs CLI and daemon sessions for
all four against Python (identical envelopes but for the rendered pages,
bytes and hash, identical errors, files, saved and filed markers and tables;
all served by Rust); the model tests are listed in the design document. The
rollout table there tracks the remaining reports.
